questions.question: Give a detailed introduction to the Holy Quran.
questions.answer: The word "Quran" literally means "to read" or "the book read". In Islamic terminology, the Holy Quran stands for the speech of Allah revealed on the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), the last of all Prophets, through the angel Jibraeel (Gabriel), and written down in the book. The Holy Quran contains 30 parts (Parahs), 114 Chapters (Surahs), 558 units (Rukus) and 6236 verses (Ayat). It begins with Surah al-Fatiha and ends with Surah an-Naas. The longest surah is Surah al-Baqarah and the shortest is Surah al-Kawthar. The longest verse, containing the glory and majesty of Almighty Allah, is Ayat al-Kursi. A Surah contains a minimum of three verses. Every surah has its own theme and topic and begins with Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim except Surah al-Tawbah. "Ayat" literally means a sign or symbol; in Islamic terminology a particular phrase of the Holy Quran ended with the 'o' symbol is called an Ayat. The Quran is Allah's eternal and everlasting speech, preserved in the Preserved Tablet (Loh-e-Mahfooz), as Allah says: "Nay! This is a Glorious Quran, inscribed in Al-Lauh Al-Mahfuz (the Preserved Tablet)" (Al-Burooj: 21-22). It was revealed to the earth in two stages: first, it was revealed wholly in "Bait al-Izzat" (the nearest heaven of the world), and second, the angel Jibraeel brought its verses and chapters to the Holy Prophet gradually, as and when needed, over a period of twenty-two years and a few months — twelve years and a few months in Makkah before the migration and the rest in Madinah after the migration. On the basis of revelation, the surahs are classified into Makki (88 surahs revealed before migration) and Madani (26 surahs revealed after migration). The Holy Quran also has several qualitative names such as Al-Quran, Al-Furqan, Al-Zikr, Al-Kitab, Al-Huda, Al-Noor, Al-Haqq, Al-Shifaa' and Al-Tanzeel.
questions.explanation: Based on the lesson's definition, statistics, revelation and naming sections (book pages 1-3, images 4-6).

questions.question: Describe some of the merits of the Holy Quran.
questions.answer: The Holy Quran is the last revealed book of Almighty Allah and the last message of guidance for human beings. It is a guidebook for all the nations of the world and a guarantee for success in this world and the Hereafter. There is no parallel to this great bounty of Allah: its recitation and listening are sources of reward, and its understanding and reflection upon its verses is a cause of the goodness of both worlds. Obedience to its teachings, preaching it to others, and conveying its message to people deprived of its blessings is a great virtue and a source of success in both worlds. It is a book free of any doubt — Allah says: "This is the Book (the Quran), whereof there is no doubt" (al-Baqarah: 2). It was revealed in the Arabic language so that people may understand it, and it has been read for centuries as it was read at the time of its revelation. Its greatest merit is that it is the Word of Allah; it is unique in its style, very attractive, and has great power to influence hearts, with no contradiction in its themes and meanings — which is itself evidence of its veracity. It is protected by Allah from corruption: "Verily We: It is We Who have sent down the Dhikr (the Quran) and surely, We will guard it (from corruption)" (Al-Hijr: 9). It is also a complete code of life covering the physical, spiritual, religious and worldly needs of all human beings, and a permanent and universal law.
questions.explanation: Drawn from the "Excellence and Virtues" and "Some merits" sections (book pages 4-5, images 7-8).

questions.question: Write down a note on the virtues of the Holy Quran.
questions.answer: The greatest virtue of the Holy Quran is that it is the Word of Allah, free from mistake, manipulation and tampering, for as Allah is Glorious, Magnificent and free of all defects, so is His Book. It is unique in its style; it is very attractive and has great power to influence hearts, and there is no contradiction in its themes and meanings, which is evidence of its veracity. The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: "The superiority of the Holy Quran over the rest of the speeches is like the superiority of Allah over the creature" (Shu'ab al-Iman, al-Baihaqi, Hadith No. 2208). The Quran is superior to all other speech just as Allah is superior to the whole of the universe. It is a book free of any doubt, and it is a complete code of life for the physical, spiritual, religious and worldly needs of all human beings — a permanent and universal law that guides us in all spheres of life. It contains guidelines about the reality of human life, lawful and unlawful, good and bad, piety and worship, and also gives Shariah rulings and principles of politics, trade, war and peace, thereby providing the means of transforming social, economic, political and moral affairs. Because of this excellence, a Muslim is required to believe in it, recite it with ablution, understand its teachings, follow them, pass them on to others, and strive for the implementation of its system in individual and social life.
questions.explanation: Summarised from the "Excellence and Virtues of the Holy Quran" section and the rights and manners section (book pages 4-6, images 7-9).

questions.question: Define the word "Quran".
questions.answer: Literally, the word "Quran" means "to read" or "the book read". In Islamic terminology, the Holy Quran stands for the speech of Allah revealed on the Holy Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) through the angel Jibraeel and written down in the book.
questions.explanation: Given in the "Introduction to the Holy Quran" definition (book page 1, image 4).

questions.question: Define the Surah and Ayat.
questions.answer: A Surah is a chapter of the Holy Quran which contains a minimum of three verses; every surah has its own theme and begins with Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim except Surah al-Tawbah. An Ayat literally means a sign or symbol, and in Islamic terminology a particular phrase of the Holy Quran, ended with the 'o' symbol, is called an Ayat. The Quran has 114 Surahs and 6236 Ayat.
questions.explanation: From the definitions in the introduction section (book page 1, image 4).

questions.question: Write down the difference between Makki and Madani Surahs.
questions.answer: The Ayat and Surahs revealed before the migration to Madinah are called Makki (88 in number) and those revealed after the migration are called Madani (26 in number). Makki Surahs are generally shorter and mainly deal with beliefs such as the Oneness of Allah, Prophethood and the Hereafter, along with worship and the stories of previous nations and prophets; they address the believers and the polytheists and mostly use "Ya ayyuhan-nas" (O people!). Madani Surahs are longer and contain detailed Shariah rulings such as Zakat, Jihad, war and criminal laws, and also explain social, economic and domestic issues; they address the Muslims, the hypocrites and the People of the Book (Ahl-e-Kitab), and mostly use "Ya ayyuhal-lazina amanu" (O you who believe!).
questions.explanation: Based on the characteristics of Makki and Madani Surahs (book pages 3-4, images 6-7).

questions.question: Write down the famous names of the Holy Quran.
questions.answer: Besides its original name "Al-Quran", the Holy Quran has several famous qualitative names mentioned in the Quran itself: Al-Quran (its original and own name), Al-Furqan (the book that differentiates between right and wrong), Al-Zikr (the book of advice), Al-Kitab (the particular book of Almighty Allah), Al-Huda (the book of guidance), Al-Noor (the book of light), Al-Haqq (the proven book, i.e. truth), Al-Shifaa' (the book which heals physical and spiritual diseases), and Al-Tanzeel (the revealed book).
questions.explanation: From "The Names of the Holy Quran" (book pages 1-2, images 4-5).

questions.question: Narrate at least two Ahadith regarding the virtues of the Holy Quran.
questions.answer: First, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: "Khairukum man ta'allamal-Qur'ana wa 'allamahu" — "The best among you is he who learns the Quran and teaches it" (Sahih Bukhari, Hadith No. 5027). Second, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: "The superiority of the Holy Quran over the rest of the speeches is like the superiority of Allah over the creature" (Shu'ab al-Iman, al-Baihaqi, Hadith No. 2208). A third narration states that the Prophet left behind two things — the Holy Quran and his Sunnah — and whoever follows them will never go astray (Mustadrik Hakim, Hadith No. 4321).
questions.explanation: The lesson quotes these Ahadith in the virtues section (book pages 4-5, image 7).

questions.question: Describe the rights and manners of the Holy Quran.
questions.answer: The Holy Quran is a sacred book whose glory is greater than the rest of the books, so Muslims must observe certain rights and manners regarding it: to believe in the Holy Quran; to recite it carefully with ablution; to understand its teachings and reflect on its verses; to follow its teachings; to pass on its teachings to others; and to struggle for the implementation of its system in individual and social life. Therefore we should live according to its teachings and follow them wholeheartedly.

chapters.title: The Translation and Explanation of the Selected Verses

questions.question: Translate the following verses. • وَآتُوا الْيَتَامَى أَمْوَالَهُمْ وَلَا تَتَبَدَّلُوا الْخَبِيثَ بِالطَّيِّبِ وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَهُمْ إِلَى أَمْوَالِكُمْ إِنَّهُ كَانَ حُوبًا كَبِيرًا • وَآتُوا النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ نِحْلَةً فَإِنْ طِبْنَ لَكُمْ عَنْ شَيْءٍ مِنْهُ نَفْسًا فَكُلُوهُ هَنِيئًا مَرِيئًا
questions.answer: Translation of the first verse (Surah al-Nisa: 2): "And give unto orphans their property and do not exchange (your) bad things for (their) good ones; and devour not their substance (by adding it) to your substance. Surely, this is a great sin." Translation of the second verse (Surah al-Nisa: 4): "And give to the women (whom you marry) their Mahr (obligatory bridal money given by the husband to his wife at the time of marriage) with a good heart, but if they, of their own good pleasure, remit any part of it to you, take it, and enjoy it without fear of any harm (as Allah has made it lawful).". The first verse commands guardians to hand over to the orphans their inherited property and warns against mixing, exchanging or consuming it unjustly, declaring this a great sin. The second verse commands husbands to pay the Mahr to their wives willingly, and permits them to use whatever the wives voluntarily give up.
questions.explanation: Translations are exactly as given in the lesson (book pages 11-12, images 14-15).

questions.question: In the light of the verse لَيْسَ الْبِرَّ write down important types of al-Birr.
questions.answer: Al-Birr means virtue and denotes the doing of righteous deeds; a Hadith says "Al-birru husnul-khuluq" — Birr is the name of good morals. In the light of the verse "Laisal-birra an tuwallu wujuhakum qibala al-mashriqi wal-maghrib" (al-Baqarah: 177), al-Birr is not merely turning faces towards the east or the west in prayer. The important types (components) of al-Birr mentioned in this verse are: (1) Beliefs — the one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the Angels, the Book and the Prophets; (2) Financial sacrifice — giving wealth, in spite of love for it, to the kinsfolk, the orphans, Al-Masakin (the poor), the wayfarer, and those who ask, and to set slaves free; (3) Worship — performing As-Salat (Iqamat-as-Salat) and giving the Zakat; and (4) Righteous conduct and morals — fulfilling the covenant when one makes it, and remaining patient (As-Sabirin) in extreme poverty, in ailment (disease), and at the time of fighting during battles. Those who possess these qualities are the people of truth and they are Al-Muttaqun (the pious). Hence true righteousness combines sound faith with good deeds, worship and good morals.
questions.explanation: Verse and its explanation given in the lesson (book pages 8-9, images 11-12).

questions.question: Write down the translation of the following verses. • وَلْيَخْشَ الَّذِينَ لَوْ تَرَكُوا مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّةً ضِعَافًا خَافُوا عَلَيْهِمْ فَلْيَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَلْيَقُولُوا قَوْلًا سَدِيدًا • إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَأْكُلُونَ أَمْوَالَ الْيَتَامَى ظُلْمًا إِنَّمَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ نَارًا وَسَيَصْلَوْنَ سَعِيرًا
questions.answer: Translation of the first verse (Surah al-Nisa: 9): "And let those (executors and guardians) have the same fear in their minds as they would have for their own, if they had left weak offspring behind. So let them fear Allah and speak right words." Translation of the second verse (Surah al-Nisa: 10): "Verily, those who unjustly eat up the property of orphans, they eat up only a fire into their bellies, and they will be burnt in the blazing Fire!". The first verse urges guardians to treat the orphans with the same care and fear they would wish for their own children, and to speak to them gently and rightly. The second verse warns those who unjustly consume the orphans' property that they are only filling fire into their bellies and will be burnt in the blazing Fire.
questions.explanation: Translations are exactly as given in the lesson (book pages 18-19, images 21-22).

questions.question: Write down the rights of the orphans in the light of verse no. 6 of Surah al-Nisa.
questions.answer: Surah al-Nisa, verse 6 ("Wabtalu al-yatama hatta iza balaghu al-nikah...") lays down the rights of the orphans and the conditions and time of handing over their property. The rights and instructions are: (1) Test/try the orphans (as regards their intelligence) until they reach the age of marriage (buloogh); (2) If sound judgement (rushd) — the ability to handle financial and business matters — is found in them, release and hand over their property to them; (3) Do not consume their property wastefully or hastily, fearing that they may grow up and demand it; (4) Among the guardians, whoever is rich should take no wages from the orphans' property, but if he is poor, he may take for himself what is just and reasonable according to his work; (5) When releasing their property to them, take witnesses in their presence to avoid future blame, misunderstanding and quarrels; and (6) Allah is All-Sufficient in taking account. Thus the verse secures both the wealth and the welfare of the orphans and fixes the manner of its safe return.
questions.explanation: Based on the explanation of Surah al-Nisa: 6 with the terms Buloogh and Rushd (book pages 15-16, images 18-19).

questions.question: Write down the translation of any two verses. • يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُمْ بَيْنَكُمْ بِالْبَاطِلِ إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً عَنْ تَرَاضٍ مِنْكُمْ وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ بِكُمْ رَحِيمًا • مِنْ أَجْلِ ذَلِكَ كَتَبْنَا عَلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ أَنَّهُ مَنْ قَتَلَ نَفْسًا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ النَّاسَ جَمِيعًا
questions.answer: Translation of the first verse (Surah al-Nisa: 29): "O you who believe! Eat not up your property among yourselves unjustly except it be a trade amongst you, by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves (nor kill one another). Surely, Allah is Most Merciful to you." Translation of the second verse (Surah al-Ma'idah: 32): "Because of that We ordained for the Children of Israel that if anyone killed a person not in retaliation of murder, or (and) to spread mischief in the land — it would be as if he killed all mankind; and if anyone saved a life, it would be as if he saved the life of all mankind...". The first verse forbids unlawful consumption of wealth and the killing of one's own self or others. The second verse declares the sanctity of human life, equating the killing of one innocent person with the killing of all humanity and the saving of one life with the saving of all humanity.
questions.explanation: Translations are exactly as given in the lesson (book pages 21 and 23-24, images 24 and 27).

questions.question: Why killing an innocent person is declared killing the whole of humanity?
questions.answer: The Holy Quran (al-Ma'idah: 32) declares that to kill any innocent person — one who neither killed anyone nor spread chaos in the land — is as if he killed the whole of humanity, and to save anyone's life is as if he saved the lives of the whole of humanity. The wisdom behind this is that a person kills only when he breaks up all human relations and loses sympathy for human beings from his heart, seeking only his personal benefit. Such a person disregards the sanctity and honour of human life altogether, and so his crime is regarded as an attack upon the whole of mankind rather than upon one individual. This law was not specified for the Bani Isra'eel only; it lasts for the whole of humanity till the Day of Judgement. It teaches that Islam dislikes bloodshed, chaos and anarchy, and instructs its followers in the principles of peace, patience, forbearance, mutual survival and respect for human beings.
questions.explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Ma'idah: 32 (book pages 23-24, images 26-27).

questions.question: What punishments has been prescribed by the Holy Quran for those who disturb the peace of society?
questions.answer: The Holy Quran (al-Ma'idah: 33-34) prescribes that the recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and do mischief in the land is that they shall be killed, or crucified, or their hands and their feet be cut off on the opposite sides, or be exiled from the land. That is their disgrace in this world, and a great torment is theirs in the Hereafter. These four kinds of punishment are stated so that the judge or ruler may decide the nature of every crime by his Ijtihad, keeping in view the objective that bloodshed, robbery, disorder and revolt against Islamic rule are severe crimes and should be prevented. However, the next verse gives an exception: those who repent (make toubah) and come back before they fall into the power of the Muslims — in that case Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful; their rights of Allah may be forgiven, while matters of human rights are settled with the concerned people (return of looted wealth, compensation, retaliation or forgiveness).
questions.explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Ma'idah: 33-34 (book pages 25-26, images 28-29).

questions.question: Translate any two verses from the following verses: • هُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ رَسُولَهُ بِالْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُشْرِكُونَ • الَّذِينَ إِنْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَقَامُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكَاةَ وَأَمَرُوا بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَنَهَوْا عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَلِلَّهِ عَاقِبَةُ الْأُمُورِ
questions.answer: Translation of the first verse (Surah al-Taubah: 33): "It is He Who has sent His Messenger (Muhammad) with guidance and the religion of truth (Islam), to make it superior over all religions even though the Mushrikun (polytheists, pagans, idolaters, disbelievers in the Oneness of Allah) hate (it)." Translation of the second verse (Surah al-Hajj: 41): "Those (Muslim rulers) who, if We give them power in the land, (they) order for Iqamat-as-Salat (to perform the five compulsory congregational prayers), to pay the Zakat and they enjoin Al-Ma'ruf (Islamic Monotheism and all that Islam orders one to do) and forbid Al-Munkar (disbelief, polytheism and all that Islam has forbidden). And with Allah rests the end of (all) matters." The first verse promises the dominance of Islam over all religions, and the second describes the duties and attributes of the Muslim rulers who are granted authority in the land.
questions.explanation: Translations are exactly as given in the lesson (book pages 29-32, images 32-35).

questions.question: Write the aims, objectives and attributes of the Islamic State mentioned in Surah Al-Hajj verse 41.
questions.answer: Surah al-Hajj, verse 41 describes the aims, objectives and attributes of the Islamic State through the conduct of the Muslim rulers whom Allah grants power in the land. Its aims and objectives are: (1) to establish Salat — ordering Iqamat-as-Salat, i.e. performing the five compulsory congregational prayers (the males in mosques); (2) to pay the Zakat, which is directly related to the economy of society; and (3) to enjoin Al-Ma'ruf (the good — Islamic Monotheism and all that Islam orders) and forbid Al-Munkar (the evil — disbelief, polytheism and all that Islam has forbidden), making the Quran the law of the country in all spheres of life. Its attributes and responsibilities are: to remain steadfast in faith, righteous deeds and worship, abstaining from polytheism; to provide peace and tranquillity to the people; to manage their education, health and livelihood; to create resources of livelihood and make arrangements for the needs of the people; to use their power to spread good and eliminate evil; and to enforce laws and impose punishments on those who cause disorder, so that peace and tranquillity prevail. The verse also reminds that with Allah rests the end of all matters.
questions.explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Hajj: 41 and the responsibilities of the Islamic State (book pages 32-33, images 35-36).

questions.question: A true believer should love "Allah Almighty and His Messenger - Hazrat Muhammad the last of all Prophets the most". Explain in the light of Surah Al-Tawbah verse 24.
questions.answer: Surah al-Taubah, verse 24 says: "Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your kindred, the wealth that you have gained, the commerce in which you fear a decline, and the dwellings in which you delight... are dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger, and striving hard and fighting in His Cause, then wait until Allah brings about His Decision (torment). And Allah guides not the people who are Al-Fasiqun (the rebellious, disobedient to Allah)." From this verse it is clear that for a true believer, belief in Allah, love for Allah and His Messenger and doing Jihad in the way of Allah are more important than everything else. No parents, children, spouses, relatives, wealth or home should be dearer to a Muslim than Allah and His Prophet, and no relative's love should stop him from the right path. Faith is the greatest wealth, by which a person gains benefits in this world and prepares himself for the Hereafter. Those who love Allah and His Messenger more than all else and migrate and strive with their life and wealth are honoured in the sight of Allah and are truly successful; but whoever does not love Allah and His Prophet more than everything else cannot be saved from the displeasure of Allah.
questions.explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Taubah: 24 (book pages 28-29, images 31-32).

questions.question: What are the duties of a Muslim leader after gaining power and authority? Explain.
questions.answer: According to Surah al-Hajj: 41, when the believers are given power and authority in the land their duties are as follows: (1) To establish Salat — ordering Iqamat-as-Salat, the five compulsory congregational prayers, so that man's relationship with Allah is strengthened and self-purification is achieved; (2) To pay the Zakat, which is related to the economy of society, and to create resources of livelihood and make arrangements for the needs of the people; (3) To command the good (Amr bil Ma'ruf) and forbid the evil (Nahi anil Munkar) — promoting good and virtuous deeds and encouraging those helpful to society, while stopping those responsible for disorder from evildoing, immorality and arrogance, imposing punishments and enforcing laws so that peace and tranquillity prevail; and (4) To make the Quran the law of the country in all spheres of life. In addition, the ruler must remain steadfast in faith, worship and righteous deeds, abstaining from polytheism, and use his power to spread good, eliminate evil and remain firm in fear and danger. In the early Islamic state of Madinah the Holy Prophet (PBUH) was the head under the Charter of Medina and was responsible for reconciliation among people, providing peace and tranquillity, and managing their education, health and livelihood.
questions.explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Hajj: 41 and the responsibilities of the Islamic State (book pages 32-33, images 35-36).

questions.question: Write down the meaning of the following words: النِّسَاءَ ، نِحْلَةً ، حُوبًا ، بَثَّ ، الْيَتَامَىٰ
questions.answer: النِّسَاءَ — the women. نِحْلَةً — a free gift / a bridal gift given willingly. حُوبًا — a (great) sin. بَثَّ — spread / scattered (He spread them). الْيَتَامَىٰ — the orphans.
questions.explanation: These words occur in the selected verses of Surah al-Nisa (1, 2 and 4) explained in the lesson (images 11-15).

questions.question: In the light of the verse ...state the occasions of patience.
questions.answer: In the verse of al-Birr (al-Baqarah: 177) the occasions of patience (Sabr) mentioned are: (i) in extreme poverty (al-Ba'sa), (ii) in ailment or disease (ad-Darra), and (iii) at the time of fighting during battles (hinal-Ba's). Those who remain patient on these three occasions are described as As-Sabirin and are counted among the people of truth and the Muttaqun.
questions.explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Baqarah: 177 (book pages 8-9, images 11-12).

questions.question: What does Sila-e-Rehmi means?
questions.answer: Sila-e-Rehmi means keeping good, brotherly and cordial relations with one's blood relatives (Al-Arhaam, the plural of Rihm). The Holy Prophet (PBUH) clarified that Sila-e-Rehmi does not mean keeping relations only with relatives who are good to you, but rather keeping good relations with relatives even if they break off with you.
questions.explanation: From the explanation of Al-Arhaam / Sila-e-Rehmi in Surah al-Nisa: 1 (book page 10, image 13).

questions.question: What instructions are given to the guardians regarding the property of the orphans?
questions.answer: The guardians of orphans are instructed to hand over the orphans' inherited property and wealth when they reach puberty, because their property is a trust in the guardians' hands. They must not exchange their own bad things for the orphans' good ones, must not mix or devour the orphans' wealth with their own, and must avoid wasting or consuming it unjustly. Violating the rights of orphans is a major sin and injustice in the sight of Allah (al-Nisa: 2).
questions.explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Nisa: 2 (book page 11, image 14).

questions.question: Write down the meaning of the following words: فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ ، فَادْفَعُوا ، ذُرِّيَّةً ، خَافُوا ، سَعِيرًا
questions.answer: فَلْيَسْتَعْفِفْ — let him abstain (from consuming the orphans' wealth) / let him be chaste and self-restrained. فَادْفَعُوا — hand over / deliver (their property to them). ذُرِّيَّةً — offspring / children. خَافُوا — they feared / had fear for them. سَعِيرًا — blazing Fire (of Hell).
questions.explanation: These words occur in the selected verses of Surah al-Nisa (6, 9 and 10) explained in the lesson (images 18-22).

questions.question: What do Buloogh and Rushd mean?
questions.answer: Buloogh means to reach the age of marriage (puberty). Rushd means to be able to handle financial and business matters, i.e. sound judgement and the ability to manage and invest property lawfully.
questions.explanation: Definitions given with the explanation of Surah al-Nisa: 6 (book page 15, image 18).

questions.question: What method is instructed in the Holy Quran about handing over the orphans' property to them?
questions.answer: The Holy Quran instructs that the orphans should first be tested until they reach the age of marriage (buloogh); if sound judgement (rushd) and the ability to manage property are found in them, their property should be handed over to them. At the time of handing over, witnesses should be arranged in their presence to avoid any blame, misunderstanding or future quarrel, and the guardian must not consume it wastefully. When this method is followed, the property is returned safely and the orphan's rights are protected.
questions.explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Nisa: 6 (book pages 15-16, images 18-19).

questions.question: What responsibilities of the guardians of the orphans are told in the Holy Quran?
questions.answer: The guardians are responsible for protecting and managing the orphans' property as a trust, not consuming or wasting it, not mixing their own wealth with it, and handing it over to the orphans when they reach puberty and sound judgement. They must also fulfil the orphans' basic needs — catering, clothing, education and training — and speak to them kindly and justly (al-Nisa: 5 and 6); a rich guardian takes no wages while a poor guardian may take only what is just and reasonable.
questions.explanation: From the explanations of Surah al-Nisa: 5 and 6 (book pages 13-16, images 16-19).

questions.question: What punishment has been declared for those who eat up the property of the orphan?
questions.answer: The Holy Quran declares that those who unjustly eat up the property of orphans are eating only fire into their bellies, and they will be burnt in the blazing Fire (al-Nisa: 10). A Hadith also counts eating up the orphans' property among the major sins (Sahih Bukhari, Hadith No. 6857).
questions.explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Nisa: 10 (book pages 18-19, images 21-22).

questions.question: Write down the meaning of the following words: لَا تَأْكُلُوا ، مُخْتَالًا ، مُسْرِفُونَ ، خِزْيٌ ، تَقْدِرُوا
questions.answer: لَا تَأْكُلُوا — do not eat up / do not devour. مُخْتَالًا — a boastful, proud person. مُسْرِفُونَ — transgressors / those who exceed the limits (set by Allah). خِزْيٌ — disgrace / humiliation. تَقْدِرُوا — you overpower them / get hold of them.
questions.explanation: These words occur in the selected verses (al-Nisa 29, 36 and al-Ma'idah 32, 34) explained in the lesson (images 24-28).

questions.question: Why the protection of the property of orphans is necessary?
questions.answer: The protection of the orphans' property is necessary because wealth is the source of livelihood and survival, and orphans are weak and unable to guard it. Wealth is indispensable for life; any minor negligence can harm the property and its owner. Therefore the Quran commands guardians to protect and manage it honestly, provide for the orphans' needs from it, and hand it over to them when they reach maturity.
questions.explanation: From the explanations of Surah al-Nisa: 5-6 and 10 (book pages 13-19, images 16-22).

questions.question: Write down the meaning of "do not kill yourself".
questions.answer: "Do not kill yourself" (wa la taqtulu anfusakum) means do not kill one another and do not destroy yourselves without any just reason. The murder of an innocent person is unlawful; considering the killing of someone as self-killing denotes that whenever a person kills someone, he will also be killed in retaliation. This verse therefore also prohibits suicide, and self-killing is regarded as worse than being killed in retaliation.
questions.explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Nisa: 29 (book page 22, image 25).

questions.question: What are the unlawful means of earning?
questions.answer: The unlawful means of earning include acquiring and using unlawful things such as pork, liquor and drugs; acquiring even lawful things by unlawful means such as theft, robbery, dacoity, violation of rights, bribery and interest (riba); and earning through lying, fraud, hoarding, black marketing, hedging, gambling, blending and short measuring. All these are forbidden, and wealth earned through transactions made with mutual consent is lawful.
questions.explanation: From the "Eating Up the Property Unlawfully" section explaining Surah al-Nisa: 29 (book page 21, image 24).

questions.question: Write the meanings of the following words: اقْتَرَفْتُمْ ، كَرِهَ ، صَوَامِعُ ، بِيعَةٌ ، مَكَّنَّا
questions.answer: اقْتَرَفْتُمْ — you have earned / committed (the wealth you have gained). كَرِهَ — he/they disliked (hated). صَوَامِعُ — monasteries / abbeys. بِيعَةٌ — churches. مَكَّنَّا — We gave (them) power / control (in the land).
questions.explanation: These words occur in the selected verses (al-Taubah 24, 33 and al-Hajj 40, 41) explained in the lesson (images 31-36).

questions.question: What should be the criterion of the love of Allah Almighty and Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) - the last of all Prophets?
questions.answer: The criterion of the love of Allah and His Messenger is that they should be dearer to a believer than everything else — parents, children, spouses, other relatives, wealth, commerce and homes. No relative or possession should stop him from the right path, and this love should be expressed by striving (Jihad) in the way of Allah. One who does not love Allah and His Prophet more than all else cannot be saved from the displeasure of Allah (al-Taubah: 24).
questions.explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Taubah: 24 (book pages 28-29, images 31-32).

questions.question: Explain the wisdom of Jihad in the light of the Holy Qur'an.
questions.answer: According to Surah al-Hajj: 39-40 and the lesson's explanation, the wisdom of Jihad includes: to defend the Islamic state and society and give permission to fight to those who have been wronged; to help the oppressed; to punish the criminals, the ungrateful and those who break their vows; to protect lives, property, honour, religion and places of worship (mosques, churches, synagogues, monasteries) from mischief; to bring peace and tranquillity in the world; and to strive for the exaltation of the word of Allah Almighty.
questions.explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Hajj: 39-40 (book pages 30-32, images 33-35).

questions.question: How was the condition of Muslims in the Makkan era?
questions.answer: In the Makkan era the condition of the Muslims was very patient and challenging. For the first thirteen years, from the proclamation of the Prophethood in Makkah to the migration to Madinah, both the Muslims and the Holy Prophet (PBUH) suffered severe hardships and oppression at the hands of the opponents. Rather than reacting to these hardships, patience and forbearance were commanded to them, and every kind of retaliation was prevented.
questions.explanation: From the explanation of Surah al-Hajj: 39-40 (book page 31, image 34).

questions.question: What is meant by Amr bil Maroof wa Nahi anil Munkar?
questions.answer: Amr bil Maroof wa Nahi anil Munkar means commanding (enjoining) the good and forbidding the evil. "Ma'ruf" (Maroof) means good and virtuous deeds which are considered praiseworthy by all, and "Munkar" means all kinds of evil or wickedness which everyone considers abominable. Good deeds should be promoted in society and people who are helpful to society should be encouraged; while those responsible for the deterioration and disorder of society should be stopped from evildoing, wickedness, immorality and arrogance, with punishments imposed and laws enforced so that peace and tranquillity prevail in society.
questions.explanation: From the "Commanding the good and forbidding the evil" section explaining Surah al-Hajj: 41 (book page 33, image 36).

questions.question: Write down some forms of assistance from Allah Almighty.
questions.answer: The forms of assistance from Allah Almighty mentioned in these verses include: Allah's promise to give victory to the believers who have been wronged (al-Hajj: 39); Allah's protection of the believers against the oppressors who are the enemies of Islam (al-Hajj: 38); Allah's granting of power and authority in the land to the believers (al-Hajj: 41); Allah's help to those who help His cause — "Truly, Allah will help those who help His (Cause)" (al-Hajj: 40); and the promise that He will make the religion of truth (Islam) superior over all other religions (al-Taubah: 33).
questions.explanation: From the explanations of Surah al-Hajj: 39-41 and Surah al-Taubah: 33 (book pages 30-33, images 33-36).

questions.question: وَالْمُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِهِمْ إِذَا عَاهَدُوا is related to:
questions.answer: (b) conduct.
questions.explanation: In al-Baqarah: 177 this phrase (those who fulfil their covenant) is part of the righteous conduct and morals mentioned, alongside beliefs, financial sacrifice and worship.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) beliefs (b) conduct (c) financial worship (d) worship

questions.question: By the words يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ the address has been directed to:
questions.answer: (b) human beings.
questions.explanation: "Ya ayyuhan-nas" (O mankind!) addresses all human beings; the lesson explains that by these words all human beings are addressed as Allah is the Creator of all (book page 10).
questions.optionsRaw: (a) angels (b) human beings (c) animals (d) jinns

questions.question: الْبِرُّ وَحُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ means:
questions.answer: (c) righteousness is the name of good morals.
questions.explanation: The lesson quotes the Hadith "Al-birru husnul-khuluq" — Birr (righteousness) is the name of good morals (book page 9, image 12).

questions.answer: (b) witness.
questions.explanation: Surah al-Nisa: 6 commands that when the property is released to the orphans, witnesses be taken in their presence (book pages 18-19).
questions.optionsRaw: (a) Advocate (b) witness (c) assistant (d) ruler

questions.answer: (a) puberty and ability.
questions.explanation: The orphans are tested for buloogh (age of marriage) and rushd (sound judgement / ability to manage property) before their property is released (book page 15).
questions.optionsRaw: (a) puberty and ability (b) health and disease (c) knowledge and intelligence (d) patience and forbearance

questions.answer: (d) the guardian is needy.
questions.explanation: The lesson states that if the guardian is needy he can take as per need with justice, whereas a wealthy guardian takes nothing (book page 16).
questions.optionsRaw: (a) the guardian is poor (b) the guardian is wealthy (c) the guardian is a debtor (d) the guardian is needy

questions.answer: (b) softly.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains that orphans should be talked to softly and politely, not harshly, and Allah commands speaking to them words of kindness and justice (book page 18).
questions.optionsRaw: (a) harshly (b) softly (c) angrily (d) misbehaving

questions.answer: (b) Hell.
questions.explanation: Surah al-Nisa: 10 warns that such people will be burnt in the blazing Fire (Hell) (book page 18).

questions.optionsRaw: (a) dust (b) fire (c) water (d) air

questions.answer: (d) bribery.
questions.explanation: The lesson lists bribery among the unlawful means of earning, while agriculture, industry and business are lawful means (book page 21).
questions.optionsRaw: (a) agriculture (b) industry (c) business (d) bribery

questions.optionsRaw: (a) Rights of Allah (b) rights of human beings (c) rights of animals (d) rights of plants

questions.answer: (b) the whole humanity.

questions.optionsRaw: (a) the whole universe (b) the whole humanity (c) the whole animal kingdom (d) the whole family

questions.answer: (b) Worship.

questions.answer: (d) suppression of Infidels.

questions.answer: (a) compulsion.

questions.answer: (d) religious enmity.

questions.optionsRaw: (a) national enmity (b) tribal enmity (c) political enmity (d) religious enmity

questions.answer: (b) of the rulers.
questions.explanation: Surah al-Hajj: 41 mentions these as the duties of the Muslim rulers who, if given power in the land, establish Salat, pay Zakat and enjoin good and forbid evil (book pages 32-33).
questions.optionsRaw: (a) of the Scholars (b) of the rulers (c) of the Mujahideen (d) of the teachers

chapters.title: Introduction to Hadith and Sunnah and Their Effects on Practical Life

questions.question: Write an essay on Hadith and Sunnah.
questions.answer: Hadith literally means news, conversation or something new. In Islamic terminology the narration of the sayings, actions and silent approvals (Taqrir) of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is called Hadith; it is also called Khabar and Sunnah. The persons through whom these narrations reached us are the narrators, the chain of narrators is Sanad-e-Hadith and the text is Matn. Sunnah literally means method or path, and in Islamic terminology it is the chosen path of the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) by which he lived his life and which he repeated. The Holy Qur'an has described this Sunnah as 'Uswa-e-Hasana' (the best role model): 'Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example' (Surah Al-Ahzab: 21). Hadith and Sunnah have the greatest importance in Islam. Just as complete belief in the Oneness of Allah is necessary, belief in the Prophethood of the Holy Prophet is equally essential, and believing in him means fulfilling the commands of Allah by following his Uswa-e-Hasana. Allah commands: 'Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you from, leave it' (Surah Al-Hashr: 7). Hadith and Sunnah are, in fact, the interpretation and explanation of the commandments of the Holy Qur'an; without Prophetic interpretation we cannot learn the number of Rak'ats of prayer, its principles and details of recitation, what should be avoided while fasting, the specific amount of wealth on which Zakat is payable, or how to perform the rituals of Hajj. The Companions were foremost in obeying the Prophet and following his Sunnah, and in a Hadith the Prophet said that whoever holds fast to his Sunnah during the turmoil of the Ummah will have the reward of a hundred martyrs. Therefore, for our success in both worlds, we must learn the Hadith and Sunnah, act upon them and follow the blessed example of the Holy Prophet in every aspect of our life.
questions.explanation: The lesson defines Hadith and Sunnah, calls the Sunnah 'Uswa-e-Hasana', quotes Surah Al-Ahzab 21 and Surah Al-Hashr 7, and explains that Hadith/Sunnah interpret the Qur'an and must be followed.

questions.question: Write a note on the types of Hadith.
questions.answer: Hadith is divided into four types. (1) Verbal Hadith (Qawli): It consists of the saying or order of the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) coming from his blessed tongue, such as 'Promote greeting (amongst you)' (Sunan al-Tirmizi, Hadith: 1854). (2) Actual Hadith (Fi'li): It consists of the actions and methods adopted by the Holy Prophet; for example, Hazrat Anas states that the Holy Prophet milked a goat himself, drank it and then rinsed his mouth with water (Sunan Ibn Majah, Hadith: 99). (3) Silent Approval Hadith (Taqriri): It refers to actions done by a companion in the presence of the Holy Prophet, or actions about which he came to know, where he neither forbade nor praised the act but remained silent, thereby giving permission or expressing consent; for example, the Holy Prophet did not forbid Hazrat Anas's younger brother Abu Umair, who kept a bird (Bulbul) and used to play with it (Sahih Bukhari: 6129, Sahih Muslim: 2150). (4) Hadith Qudsi (Sacred Hadith): It is a Hadith in which the meaning and connotation are from Allah Almighty while the words are of the Holy Prophet, such as 'O son of Adam! Spend (on my servants) and I will spend on you' (Sahih Bukhari: 5352).
questions.explanation: The lesson lists exactly these four types (Qawli/verbal, Fi'li/actual, Taqriri/silent approval, Qudsi) with the examples quoted above.

questions.question: Write a note on the effects of Sunnah on our life.
questions.answer: The Sunnah of the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) has very significant effects on human life. First, since man must fulfil his everyday needs and deeds, if he performs them according to the Sunnah they are counted as acts of worship; for example, at the time of a meal, following the Sunnah, people sit together, spread the tablecloth and arrange a collective meal, and then this ordinary meal also becomes an act of worship. Second, following the Sunnah brings betterment of human health and of the environment, because the Sunnah teaches the use of Halal (lawful) and desirable things as well as purification and cleanliness, which prevent all kinds of diseases. Third, following the Sunnah creates unity and solidarity and overcomes differences; a common code of practical life for all people weakens their tendency to disagree. Fourth, following the Sunnah prevents a person from all evils and the false paths of Satan, promotes an environment of truth and goodness and averts all social and moral evils. Fifth, science has also supported the Sunnah in many issues of life, although the Sunnah does not need the support of science at all. Thus the Sunnah reforms our worship, our health, our environment, our society and our morals, and leads us to success in both worlds.
questions.explanation: The lesson enumerates these effects of the Sunnah on practical life: deeds becoming worship, betterment of health and environment, unity and solidarity, protection from evil, and support by science.

questions.question: What is meant by Sunnah? Write in the light of the Holy Qur'an.
questions.answer: The literal meanings of the word 'Sunnah' are 'method' and 'path'. In Islamic terminology, the chosen path of the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) by which he lived his life, and which he repeated, is called Sunnah. In the light of the Holy Qur'an, Allah has described the Sunnah as 'Uswa-e-Hasana' (the best role model): 'Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example' (Surah Al-Ahzab: 21).
questions.explanation: The lesson gives the literal meanings of Sunnah as method/path and cites Surah Al-Ahzab 21 where the Sunnah is called Uswa-e-Hasana.

questions.question: Write the literal and terminological meaning of "Hadith".
questions.answer: The literal meaning of the word 'Hadith' is news, conversation and something new. In Islamic terminology, the narration of the sayings, actions and silent approvals (Taqrir) of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is called Hadith. It is also called 'Khabar' (news/story) and 'Sunnah'.
questions.explanation: This is the lesson's opening definition of Hadith, including its other names Khabar and Sunnah.

questions.question: What are the literal and terminological meanings of "Sunnah"?
questions.answer: The literal meanings of the word 'Sunnah' are 'method' and 'path'. In Islamic terminology, the chosen path of the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) by which he lived his life, and that action which he repeated, is called Sunnah.
questions.explanation: The lesson defines Sunnah literally as method/path and technically as the Prophet's chosen, repeated way of living.

questions.question: "Uswa" is the word of which language, and what does it literally mean?
questions.answer: 'Uswa' is an Arabic word and it literally means a model, example or pattern to be followed. The Holy Qur'an has described the Sunnah of the Holy Prophet as 'Uswa-e-Hasana', that is, the best role model for the believers.
questions.explanation: The lesson uses 'Uswa-e-Hasana' (the best role model) as the Qur'anic description of the Prophet's Sunnah; Uswa is the Arabic word for an example/role model.

questions.question: What is Matn-e-Hadith?
questions.answer: The text, that is the actual wording of a Hadith apart from its chain of narrators, is called 'Matn' (content). Hence Matn-e-Hadith means the content or text portion of the Hadith.
questions.explanation: The lesson states that the text of a Hadith is called 'Matn' (content), as distinct from the Sanad (chain of narrators).

questions.question: Explain Sanad-e-Hadith.
questions.answer: Sanad-e-Hadith is the chain of narrators through which a Hadith has been transmitted from the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) to us. The persons who narrate the Ahadith are called narrators, and their connected sequence is called the Sanad.
questions.explanation: The lesson defines Sanad-e-Hadith as the chain of narrators by which the Hadith reaches us.

questions.question: What is the meaning of "narrator"?
questions.answer: A narrator (Rawi) is the person who narrates or transmits a Hadith from the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) to us. The chain formed by these narrators is called Sanad-e-Hadith.
questions.explanation: The lesson says those who have narrated the Ahadith from the Holy Prophet to us are called narrators, and the chain of narrators is the Sanad-e-Hadith.

questions.question: Hadith: "Whosoever holds fasts to my Sunnah during the turmoil of my Ummah, for him there is a reward of a hundred martyrs", explain it.
questions.answer: In this Hadith the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) gives glad tidings that whoever adheres firmly to his Sunnah at a time when the Ummah is passing through turmoil, disorder and trials, and who keeps acting upon the Prophet's way despite the corruption around him, will be granted the reward of a hundred martyrs. It shows the great merit and excellence of following the Sunnah and remaining steadfast upon it during difficult times (Hilyat ul Awliya by Isfahani: vol. 8, p. 200).
questions.explanation: The lesson quotes this Hadith while stressing the importance of Hadith and Sunnah, promising the reward of a hundred martyrs to those who hold fast to the Sunnah in the turmoil of the Ummah.

questions.question: Literal meaning of Sunnah is:
questions.answer: path. The lesson explains that the literal meanings of the word 'Sunnah' are 'method' and 'path'.
questions.explanation: The lesson states the literal meaning of Sunnah is 'path' and 'method'.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) Conversation (b) law (c) Custom and tradition (d) path

questions.question: The Hadith, in which the meaning and connotation are from Allah Almighty and the words are of the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) is called:
questions.answer: Qudsi. Hadith Qudsi (Sacred Hadith) is that Hadith in which the meaning and connotation are from Allah Almighty while the words are of the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him).
questions.explanation: The lesson defines Hadith Qudsi as the Hadith whose meaning is from Allah and whose words are the Prophet's.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) Taqriri (b) actual (c) verbal (d) Qudsi

questions.question: The word expresses the meaning of Hadith is:
questions.answer: Sunnah. The lesson states that the Hadith is also called 'Khabar' (news/story) and 'Sunnah', so Sunnah is the word that is used to express the meaning of Hadith.
questions.explanation: The lesson says the Hadith is also called Sunnah (and Khabar), i.e., the same reality is expressed by the word Sunnah.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) Sunnah (b) wisdom (c) Qiyas (Analogy) (d) Ij'ma (consensus)

chapters.title: Translation and Explanation of Selected Ahadith

questions.question: Translate the following Ahadith: (1) خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ (2) أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَكْثَرُهُمْ عَلَىَّ صَلَاةً
questions.answer: (1) خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ — "The best amongst you is the one who learns the Qur'an and teaches it to others." (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith: 5027). (2) أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَكْثَرُهُمْ عَلَىَّ صَلَاةً — "The nearest to me on the Day of Resurrection will be those who invoke blessings on me (send the most Durood) extensively." (Sunan al-Tirmizi, Hadith: 484).
questions.explanation: These are the wordings and translations of Hadith No. 1 and Hadith No. 4 of the lesson.

questions.question: Translate the following Ahadith: (1) طَلَبُ الْعِلْمِ فَرِيضَةٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ (2) اَلصَّلَاةُ عِمَادُ الدِّينِ
questions.answer: (1) طَلَبُ الْعِلْمِ فَرِيضَةٌ عَلَى كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ — "Seeking knowledge is a duty upon every Muslim." (Shih Muslim, Hadith: 224). (2) اَلصَّلَاةُ عِمَادُ الدِّينِ — "Prayer is the pillar of religion." (Al-Durar ul Muntathira fi al-Ahadith al-Mushtahira by Suyuti: p. 280).
questions.explanation: These are the wordings and translations of Hadith No. 6 and Hadith No. 7 of the lesson.

questions.question: Translate the following Ahadith: (1) أَكْمَلُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِيمَانًا أَحْسَنُهُمْ خُلُقًا (2) خَيْرُ النَّاسِ أَنْفَعُهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ (3) اَلْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْيَدِ السُّفْلَى
questions.answer: (1) أَكْمَلُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِيمَانًا أَحْسَنُهُمْ خُلُقًا — "The most perfect believers among you in respect of complete faith are those who have best morals than others." (Sunan Abu Dawood: 4682). (2) خَيْرُ النَّاسِ أَنْفَعُهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ — "The best of people is he who is the most beneficial to people." (Al-Jamiul-Kabeer by al-Suyuti, Hadith: 11760). (3) اَلْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْيَدِ السُّفْلَى — "The upper hand is better than the lower hand." (Sunan Abu Dawood: 1645).
questions.explanation: These are the wordings and translations of Hadith No. 11, Hadith No. 12 and Hadith No. 15 of the lesson.

questions.question: Write the translation and explanation of any one of the following Ahadith: (1) مَنْ حَجَّ لِلّٰہِ فَلَمْ يَرْفُثْ وَلَمْ يَفْسُقْ رَجَعَ كَيَوْمٍ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ (2) إِنَّ اللّٰهَ لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى أَجْسَادِكُمْ وَلَا إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ وَلَكِنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ
questions.answer: (Chosen Hadith No. 16) مَنْ حَجَّ لِلّٰہِ فَلَمْ يَرْفُثْ وَلَمْ يَفْسُقْ رَجَعَ كَيَوْمٍ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ — Translation: "Whoever performs Hajj for Allah's pleasure and he neither abuses nor calls names, and does not commit sin, then he will return from Hajj as if he were born anew." (Sahih al-Bukhari: 1521). Explanation: This Hadith describes the excellence of Hajj. Hajj is the last and complementary pillar of Islam, which is obligatory once in a lifetime on a sane, adult, healthy and able Muslim; it is a strong means of approaching Allah Almighty. The Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Perform Hajj and Umrah voluntarily (Nafil), for they remove poverty and sins as the bellows remove impurity from iron, gold and silver, and Hajj Al-Mabrur brings no less reward than Paradise" (Sunan An-Nisa'i: 2631). Moreover, the Hadith instructs that a person should show patience during Hajj; he should avoid immodest words, lousy speech or any nonsense act that falls within disobedience to Allah, and should refrain from illegal and unlawful acts, quarrels and sins. If, however, he seeks forgiveness for shortcomings committed in the rights of Allah and compensates for those committed in human rights, he will be cleansed of sins as on the day he was born. (Alternative: Hadith No. 19, إِنَّ اللّٰهَ لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَى أَجْسَادِكُمْ وَلَا إِلَى صُوَرِكُمْ وَلَكِنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ — "Verily, Allah Almighty does not look at your figures, nor at your faces, but He looks at your hearts" (Sahih Muslim: 2564); it teaches sincerity, i.e., that outward and inward should be the same and that every deed must be done only for Allah's pleasure.)
questions.explanation: The lesson gives both Hadith No. 16 and Hadith No. 19; the question asks for any one. The chosen answer is Hadith No. 16 (on the excellence of Hajj), with the alternative Hadith No. 19 on sincerity also supplied.

questions.question: Write the translation and explanation of any one of the following Ahadith: (1) مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ (2) إِيَّاكُمْ وَالظَّنَّ فَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ أَكْذَبُ الْحَدِيثِ
questions.answer: (Chosen Hadith No. 21) مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ — Translation: "One who guides to something good has a reward similar to that of its doer." (Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 1893). Explanation: This Hadith instructs us to do good and righteous deeds and to cooperate with one another on goodness and righteous deeds. The Holy Qur'an commands us to cooperate in righteousness and good deeds while forbidding us from helping one another in sin and disobedience (Surah al-Ma'idah: 2). Therefore, giving good advice, education and guidance to someone will be rewarded equally to the reward of the doer. Hence we should move towards goodness and righteousness ourselves and encourage others as well. (Alternative: Hadith No. 25, إِيَّاكُمْ وَالظَّنَّ فَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ أَكْذَبُ الْحَدِيثِ — "Avoid suspicion, for it is the biggest lie" (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith: 6066); it forbids unnecessary suspicion, saying something about others without research and investigation, and commands good conjecture.)
questions.explanation: The lesson gives both Hadith No. 21 and Hadith No. 25; the question asks for any one. The chosen answer is Hadith No. 21 (on guiding to good), with the alternative Hadith No. 25 on suspicion also supplied.

questions.question: Explain the Hadith: لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى أَكُونَ أَحَبَّ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ وَالِدِهِ وَوَلَدِهِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ
questions.answer: This Hadith describes love for the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) as a sign of true faith. Its translation is: "None of you truly believes until I am more beloved to him than his child, his father and all the people" (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith: 15). It means that no one can be a perfect believer unless the Holy Prophet is dearer to him than his parents, his children and all the people of the world. Love of the Prophet includes all kinds of natural love such as the love of parents, wife and children, or love due to other physical or psychological reasons. This Hadith teaches that, out of sincere love for the Prophet, a person must be willing to sacrifice his desires, his will, his wealth, his children and even his life to the commands of Allah and the Holy Prophet; only then can he be a perfect believer. This is confirmed by another Hadith in which the Prophet said: "None of you can be a (perfect) believer until his desire should not be subject to the Shariah which I have brought" (Sharh ul Sunnah by Baghawi, vol. 1, p. 212-213).
questions.explanation: Hadith No. 5 of the lesson; its explanation treats love of the Prophet as a sign of faith and ties it to the hadith about submitting one's desires to the Shariah.

questions.question: Write the explanation of the Hadith: كُلُّكُمْ رَاعٍ وَكُلُّكُمْ مَسْئُوْلٌ عَنْ رَعِيَّتِهِ
questions.answer: This Hadith, "All of you are guardians, and all of you will be questioned about your subjects" (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith: 893), declares every person a guardian (Rai). A guardian is responsible for his respective duties from a social and worldly point of view, and the people under him are called his subjects (Raiyyah). Guidance and counselling are also among the duties of a guardian; he must teach good manners to each of his subjects and keep them in good moral condition. On the Day of Resurrection every person will give an account of his own deeds, and a person who held any position or responsibility in the world will also be asked about his subordinates. The ruler will be asked about his entire nation, whether he did justice to them, fulfilled their rights and protected their lives and property; the wife will be asked about her house; the husband about his wife and children and their better care, education and upbringing; the employee or official about the related matters; and the teacher about the students in his class. Moreover, every human being will be asked about his body organs, where they were used, and whether he is entitled to reward or punishment. Therefore everyone is addressed to ensure the rights of his subordinates, to take care of the weaker sections of society and to avoid encroaching upon their rights.
questions.explanation: Hadith No. 10 of the lesson; its explanation makes every person a guardian accountable for his subjects on the Day of Resurrection.

questions.question: Write down the disadvantages of bribery in detail.
questions.answer: Bribery is the money or compensation by which one's right is violated, or the money taken in exchange for some injustice or unlawful gifts; taking and giving bribes is one of the major sins. Its disadvantages for a nation and society are very serious. Bribery becomes common in a nation when justice and morality are lost; the legitimate rights of human beings are then prevented by the unjust demands of the oppressors, and the rightful person's due right is either violated or not paid in a lawful manner. Justice is destroyed because decisions no longer rest on truth but on the payment of money, so the rich and the powerful obtain what they want while the poor and the weak are deprived. This breeds oppression, hatred and class conflict, and destroys the trust of the common man in the law and the administration. Bribery corrupts officials and the judiciary, encourages further dishonesty, greed and moral decay, and turns society into one in which merit is ignored and evil flourishes. Because it combines oppression, the violation of rights and the spread of injustice, the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) has cursed both the bribe-giver and the bribe-taker, and in another Hadith even the one who intermediates between the two is cursed (Musnad Ahmad: 22399; Sunan Nisa'i: 2631).
questions.explanation: The lesson (under Hadith No. 14) defines bribery, calls it a major sin, and explains that it spreads when justice and morality are lost and that both giver and taker (and the intermediary) are cursed.

questions.question: Write briefly on the six special mutual rights of a Muslim to another Muslim.
questions.answer: In Hadith No. 17 (Sunan Al-Tirmizi: 2736) the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) laid down six courtesies (rights) that are due from one Muslim to another Muslim: (1) to greet him with Salam when he meets him; (2) to accept his invitation when he invites him; (3) to say 'May Allah show mercy upon you' (Yarhamukallah) to him when he sneezes; (4) to visit him when he is ill; (5) to offer his funeral prayer and to go along with his funeral (Janazah) when he dies; and (6) to love for him what he loves for himself. These six rights build and develop the relationship between two Muslims, and they should be observed conscientiously in daily practical life. Allah Almighty says, "The believers are brothers to one another" (Surah al-Hujurat: 10). Islam has strengthened this relation of brotherhood and wants the love and affection of Muslims to be permanent and lasting, so that they are good to one another and valuable to the society.
questions.explanation: Hadith No. 17 of the lesson lists exactly these six rights; the explanation quotes Surah al-Hujurat 10 on Muslim brotherhood.

questions.question: Write a note on conjecture.
questions.answer: Conjecture (Zann) means saying something or forming an opinion about others without research and investigation. If it is based on a good intention it is called 'good conjecture', which is a good quality; it has been encouraged in the Hadith, and especially to have a good conjecture of Allah Almighty is an act of worship, for the Prophet said, "Indeed, having good thoughts concerning Allah Almighty is a good worship" (Musnad Ahmad, Hadith: 7956). However, if it is based on a bad intention, meaning that one doubts someone and does not consider him good in the heart for no reason, it is interpreted as suspicion, which is forbidden. The Holy Qur'an says, "O believers! Beware of suspicion, for it is the act of sin" (Surah Al-Hujurat: 12). Therefore, no matter how many bad complaints one receives about a person, one should not be suspicious of anyone until the matter is investigated, because suspicion reduces interaction and gradually turns into hatred and enmity in the hearts, which is a major sin.
questions.explanation: Hadith No. 25 and its explanation define conjecture, distinguish good conjecture from forbidden suspicion, and quote Surah Al-Hujurat 12.

questions.question: Write the virtues and importance of protecting the borders of the homeland in the light of Hadith: رِبَاطُ يَوْمٍ وَلَيْلَةٍ خَيْرٌ مِنْ صِيَامِ شَهْرٍ وَقِيَامِهِ
questions.answer: This Hadith, "Observing Ribat (voluntary defence of Islam) in the way of Allah for a day and a night is far better than observing Saum (fasting) for a whole month and standing in Salat (prayer) in all its nights" (Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 1913), mentions the virtue and importance of protecting the borders of the Islamic State. Defending and protecting the country's borders, even by making a small fortification, has also been counted as Jihad. The Hadith states that if the Mujahideen who defend the borders for one day or one night do so for the pleasure of Allah Almighty, they will get a reward better than fasting during the day and offering additional prayers (Tahajjud) at night for the whole month. This shows the excellent reward reserved for the Mujahideen and the veterans of Islamic countries who perform these good deeds for Allah's pleasure. Therefore, we should also strive to uplift the word of Allah and to protect our homeland and its borders with absolute passion, so that no one dares to glance at Islam, our honours and our country with an evil eye. This also ensures our welfare in both worlds.
questions.explanation: Hadith No. 9 of the lesson; its explanation describes Ribat as guarding the borders, counted as Jihad, with a reward greater than a month's fasting and night prayer.

questions.question: Explain the service and help of the needy and the afflicted.
questions.answer: This is taught by Hadith No. 22 (Sahih Muslim: 2699), which says that he who relieves a Muslim believer from one of the hardships of this worldly life, Allah Almighty will relieve him of one of the hardships of the Day of Resurrection; and he who finds relief for one who is depressed, Allah will make things easy for him in the Hereafter; and he who makes it easy for one who is indebted to him, Allah will make it easy for him in this worldly life and in the Hereafter. The Hadith emphasises the service and assistance of the needy, the sick and the afflicted. The Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) encouraged the fulfilment of people's needs and explained the reward of giving respite to a distressed debtor. Two factors have been clarified about human rights and social welfare: (1) if a believer is in trouble, pain or distress, it is an excellent act of worship to relieve his distress and assist him, for the Prophet said, "Allah Almighty is at the back of a servant so long as the servant is at the back of his brother" (Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 2699); and (2) if a believer is sick, destitute, poor or needy, it is a great reward to serve him and help him financially, and giving a debtor respite in his debt is also a great reward. Hence, if anyone in our society suddenly comes to a calamity, we should strive to save him from the calamity and offer our services to help him, and we should also encourage others to do the same, so that the people of our society can live a prosperous life and we obtain blessings in both worlds.
questions.explanation: Hadith No. 22 and its explanation describe the service and help of the needy and the afflicted and the reward of relieving distress and giving debtors respite.

questions.question: What is meant by the remembrance of Allah (Zikrullah)?
questions.answer: Remembrance of Allah (Zikr-e-Allah) means, in its broad sense, prayer, recitation of the Holy Qur'an, supplications and asking for forgiveness; in its specific sense it means the glorification of Allah Almighty, His Oneness, His greatness and exaltation, and the description of the perfection of His attributes.
questions.explanation: This is the lesson's definition of Zikrullah, distinguishing its broad and specific meanings.

questions.question: What are the two levels of knowledge?
questions.answer: The first is 'knowledge as exact duty', which is the duty of every man and woman to learn at least so much knowledge as is needed to recognise the essentials of faith, the lawful (Halal) and unlawful (Haraam), the pure and impure, and his or her own responsibilities. The second is 'knowledge as sufficient duty', which means acquiring complete knowledge of religion and of the worldly sciences and arts; this is a sufficient obligation (Fard Kifayah) on individual and collective levels and includes men as well as women.
questions.explanation: The lesson (under Hadith No. 6) explains these two levels of knowledge: knowledge as exact duty and knowledge as sufficient duty.

questions.question: What is meant by "good morals"?
questions.answer: Good morals (Akhlaq-e-Hasana) mean fulfilling the rules and regulations of religion in daily living, treating others well instead of hurting them, meeting them with a smile and fulfilling one's responsibilities properly. Good morals have been declared a condition of perfect faith and hold great importance in Islam.
questions.explanation: The lesson (under Hadith No. 11) defines good morals exactly in these words and links them with perfect faith.

questions.question: Write a note on the dignity of Knowledge.
questions.answer: The Hadith 'Seek knowledge even if from China' (Kanzul Ummal: 28697-28698) highlights the greatness of knowledge and its necessity. The fundamental requisite of human nature is to know every good and bad thing about himself and the universe, and man cannot progress in the world without knowledge. It is necessary to endure hard work and severity to acquire knowledge, because without these efforts there can be no maturity and excellence in knowledge. The great narrators of Hadith, scholars and scientists of the past travelled long distances and bore the hardships of travel and migration to acquire knowledge, and that is why their names are remembered with honour even today. Thus, if hardship comes in the journey of acquiring knowledge, one should bear it, and one should work hard for knowledge even if one has to travel to distant places.
questions.explanation: Hadith No. 18 and its explanation describe the dignity of knowledge and the need to bear hardship to acquire it.

questions.question: Explain the types of neighbours.
questions.answer: Three types of neighbour are presented in the Holy Qur'an (Surah Al-Nisa: 36): a neighbour who is a relative; a neighbour who is only a neighbour; and a neighbour who is staying temporarily for some time near someone, such as during travelling, in a class or at a meeting. Neighbours of all sorts should be treated well and served, whether they belong to one's own religion or to any other religion, and whether they hold the same ideology or a different one.
questions.explanation: The lesson (under Hadith No. 23) mentions these three types of neighbour by reference to Surah Al-Nisa 36.

questions.question: Why "Lā ilāha illallāh" is declared the best remembrance?
questions.answer: "Lā ilāha illallāh" ("There is none worthy of worship except Allah") is declared the best remembrance because it teaches us to believe in Allah Almighty alone and is therefore called the word of Tauheed and of faith. It is the essence of all the attributes of perfection and is the most effective in purifying the inner self and turning the heart towards Allah; by confessing and believing in it with sincerity a person enters Islam and becomes entitled to enter Paradise.
questions.explanation: The lesson states that this phrase is the best Zikr as it is the essence of all perfect attributes and purifies the inner self.

questions.question: On which factors foundation of Islam is based?
questions.answer: The foundation of Islam is based on five things: the testimony of Tauheed and Prophethood, establishing prayers, paying Zakat, fasting in the month of Ramdan and performing Hajj to Baitullah (Bukhari and Muslim).
questions.explanation: The lesson (under Hadith No. 7) quotes the Prophet's Hadith that the foundation of Islam rests on these five pillars.

questions.question: What are the qualities of a good human being?
questions.answer: As taught by the Ahadith of this section, a good human being is the one who is the most beneficial to other people and does not harm them; who fulfils the rules of religion and treats others well (good morals); who has mercy on the young and respect for the elders; who keeps away from bribery and other major sins; and who is generous, giving to others with the open (upper) hand instead of spreading his hand before others to take.
questions.explanation: The qualities are drawn from Hadith No. 11 (good morals), No. 12 (beneficial to people), No. 13 (mercy to young, respect to elders), No. 14 (avoiding bribery) and No. 15 (the giving/upper hand).

questions.question: What is meant by sincerity? Explain.
questions.answer: Sincerity (Ikhlas) means that whatever good deed is done should be done only for the pleasure of Allah Almighty and not for any worldly purpose such as showing off, seeking fame or compensation. Hadith No. 19 teaches that Allah does not look at our figures or faces but at our hearts, so a person's outward and inward should be the same, and the right intention and devotion in the heart have primary importance. If an action is done with sincerity and piety it is accepted by Allah and will be rewarded; on the contrary, if any worldly interest is intended in the action, only that worldly interest will be obtained and there will be no reward for the action in the sight of Allah in the Hereafter.
questions.explanation: The explanation of Hadith No. 19 in the lesson defines sincerity as doing every good deed solely for Allah's pleasure and stresses the condition of the heart.

questions.question: Explain honouring the guest.
questions.answer: When a person travels and reaches someone for any purpose, he is called a guest. Honouring the guest means asking about the purpose of his arrival in a proper way, treating him with a smile, arranging his accommodation, food and rest, and giving him respect. The Hadith (Sahih Al-Bukhari: 6138) makes hospitality to the guest a duty of the one who believes in Allah Almighty and the Last Day.
questions.explanation: The lesson (under Hadith No. 24) defines honouring the guest in these terms and cites the Hadith making it a duty of the believer.

questions.question: What is meant by "Du'a" (Supplication)?
questions.answer: "Du'a" is the act of asking for something from someone superior while expressing humility at the request. In Islamic Shariah, Du'a means to ask something from Allah Almighty believing in Him and requesting Him for any favour; it is a means of attaining one's goal, just as a servant makes efforts to fulfil his needs and wants.
questions.explanation: The lesson defines Du'a both linguistically and in Shariah, and calls it a means of attaining one's goal.

questions.question: Write a Hadith on the significance of Fasting.
questions.answer: The Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever observes fasts during the month of Ramdan out of sincere faith, and hoping to attain Allah's rewards, then (because of this) all his past sins will be forgiven" (Sahih Bukhari, Hadith: 38). He also said: "Fasting is a shield from the fire of Hell" (Sunan al-Nasa'i: 2224).
questions.explanation: These are the Ahadith of the lesson (Hadith No. 8) describing the significance and reward of fasting in Ramdan.

questions.question: Define bribery.
questions.answer: Bribery is the money or compensation by which one's right is violated, or the money taken in exchange for some injustice or unlawful gifts. Taking and giving bribes is one of the major sins, and bribery becomes common in a nation when justice and morality are lost.
questions.explanation: This is the lesson's definition of bribery given under Hadith No. 14.

questions.question: What are the most excellent and humble branches of faith?
questions.answer: The Hadith (Sahih Muslim, Hadith: 35) states that faith has over sixty or seventy branches. The most excellent branch is the declaration that 'There is no god but Allah' (Lā ilāha illallāh), because through it Tauheed is confessed, which is the foundation of faith. The humblest branch is the removal of what is injurious (a harmful object) from the path, because it protects the passers-by from trouble and is thus an act of reward and virtue.
questions.explanation: Hadith No. 20 of the lesson names the highest branch (Lā ilāha illallāh) and the humblest branch (removing a harmful thing from the path).

questions.question: What is meant by good relations with kin?
questions.answer: Good relations with kin (Sila-e-Rahmi) means sharing in the sorrows of one's relatives and kin, coming to their aid in time of need, treating them well and adopting a sympathetic attitude towards them. The Hadith says, "Whoever wants that he be granted more wealth and that his lease of life be prolonged, then he should keep good relations with his kin" (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith: 2067).
questions.explanation: The lesson (under Hadith No. 24) defines Sila-e-Rahmi and quotes the Hadith about its reward of more wealth and longer life.

questions.question: Who are entitled for obligation of fasting? Discuss.
questions.answer: Fasting in the month of Ramdan is obligatory upon every sane, adult, healthy and resident Muslim man and woman. Fasting became obligatory in the 2nd A.H. It is not obligatory upon the insane, the minor child, the sick person, the traveller, and a woman during her menstruation; such persons are exempt and must either make up the missed fasts later or give the due compensation as prescribed. Fasting is an excellent act of worship that creates piety in the personality, improves one's health and brings about a sense of sympathy for the needy.
questions.explanation: The lesson states that fasting is obligatory on every sane, adult, healthy and resident Muslim and explains who is exempt (Hadith No. 8 explanation).

questions.question: What is meant by modesty? Describe.
questions.answer: Modesty (Haya) is a significant branch of faith and is mentioned in the Hadith as 'the branch of faith'. It is the quality that prevents a person from immorality and from many evils and sins. A person who possesses this quality is not tempted by evil but instead moves towards good, so modesty is the source of all goodness. Therefore we should try to adopt the other branches of faith within ourselves, and mainly cultivate the quality of modesty, so that our life may be purified and clean.
questions.explanation: The explanation of Hadith No. 20 in the lesson describes modesty as a branch of faith and the source of goodness that prevents evil.

questions.question: According to a Hadith, The best remembrance is:
questions.answer: لَااِلٰہَ اِلَّا اللّٰہ. The Hadith says: "The best remembrance is 'There is none worthy of worship except Allah' (Lā ilāha illallāh)." (Sunan al-Tirmizi, Hadith: 3383).
questions.explanation: Hadith No. 2 declares 'Lā ilāha illallāh' as the best remembrance.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) سُبْحَانَ اللّٰہ (b) اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰہ (c) اَللّٰہُ اَکْبَر (d) لَااِلٰہَ اِلَّا اللّٰہ

questions.question: To acquire complete knowledge of religion is:
questions.answer: sufficient duty. The lesson calls acquiring complete knowledge of religion and of the worldly sciences a 'knowledge as sufficient duty' (Fard Kifayah).
questions.explanation: The lesson names this second level of knowledge 'knowledge as sufficient duty'.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) exact duty. (b) sufficient duty. (c) Sunnah. (d) Mustahab (preferred).

questions.question: According to the Hadith, the one who benefits people more is declared as:
questions.answer: The best of people. The Hadith says 'خَيْرُ النَّاسِ أَنْفَعُهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ' — "The best of people is he who is the most beneficial to people" (Hadith No. 12).
questions.explanation: Hadith No. 12 declares the most beneficial person 'the best of people'.
