questions.question: Write down an essay on the importance, significance and benefits of knowledge.
questions.answer: Knowledge is the greatest blessing of Almighty Allah among His exclusive favours on human beings. The first quality conferred to Prophet Adam (AS) right after his creation was knowledge, and Allah states: "And Allah the Supreme taught Adam all the names (of things)." (Surah Al-Baqarah: 31). Almighty Allah declared human beings the best creation and blessed them with wisdom and knowledge; the entire universe has been made under the control of humans through knowledge, and man has superiority over other creations due to knowledge. Knowledge is the basis of all excellence and the means of transcendence. It is itself an attribute of Allah, the Knower of all hidden things and the Knower of inside hearts. The world was unaware of the importance of knowledge when Islam began in Arabia; Islam highlighted the value of knowledge and encouraged people to acquire it. About the significance of knowledge and scholars the Holy Qur'an says: "Allah will raise the believers among you, and those given knowledge, to high ranks." (Surah Al-Mujadilah: 58,11) and "My Lord, bestow me more knowledge." (Surah Taha: 114) and "Are the knowledgeable and the ignorant equal?" (Surah Az-Zumar: 39,9). The Holy Prophet (PBUH) said: "Scholars are the heirs of Prophets." (Sunan Tirmizi: 2682); "A single knowledgeable believer is harder on Satan than a thousand devout worshippers." (Sunan Ibn-e-Majah: 222); and "To acquire knowledge is obligatory upon every Muslim (male and female)." Good morals and manners — including the distinction between right and wrong, sense of good and evil, recognition of the Creator and Master, and love and kindness with the creation — are developed in a person if he is groomed under the shade of knowledge and morality. As a result, the person gets dignified in character and habits and becomes a valuable citizen. Therefore, seeking knowledge is considered an obligation in Islam, and moral grooming of our subordinates, offspring and family is also our responsibility; knowledge and morality are indispensable to each other. In fact, the basis of all morals and other qualities is knowledge, which has to be preferred by every Muslim.
questions.explanation: Compiled from the lesson "Importance and Excellence of Knowledge", including the Qur'anic verses (Al-Baqarah 31, Al-Mujadilah 58:11, Taha 114, Az-Zumar 39:9) and Ahadith of Tirmizi and Ibn-e-Majah.

questions.question: Describe the meaning and concept of knowledge.
questions.answer: The literal meaning of "knowledge" is to know and become aware of; however, the word "education" is used to pass on knowledge to others and to teach. Terminologically, knowledge stands for knowing the reality of something through the five senses and the intellect. Knowledge is the greatest blessing of Almighty Allah, and the first quality conferred to Prophet Adam right after his creation was knowledge.
questions.explanation: Based on the section "The Concept and Meaning of Knowledge" in the lesson.

questions.question: Quote a verse along with a translation on the importance of knowledge.
questions.answer: "Allah will raise the believers among you, and those given knowledge, to high ranks." (Surah Al-Mujadilah: 58, 11). In this verse knowledge is explained along with faith as a means of elevation to high ranks. (Another verse: "And pray, My Lord, bestow me more knowledge." (Surah Taha: 114).)
questions.explanation: Verse quoted directly from the lesson's section on the significance of knowledge and scholars.

questions.question: The Holy Prophet (سم الله عليه وآله واصحابه وسلم) said that the heirs of Prophets are:
questions.answer: Scholars.
questions.explanation: The Holy Prophet said "Scholars are the heirs of Prophets" (Sunan Tirmizi: 2682), so option (a) Scholars is correct.
questions.optionsRaw: (a) Scholars (b) Aulia (c) Teachers (d) Students

questions.question: Write down a note on the significance of family in Islam.
questions.answer: The word "Khandan" (family) is a Persian word meaning a household, family, tribe, offspring and ancestry; domestic life stands for the gathering of close relatives of a clan. By nature a man cannot live all alone; he likes to live combined with the population of a house, area, village or city. Parents, husband and wife, and offspring have a crucial position in a family, and the family group extends to grandparents, paternal and maternal uncles and aunts and their offspring. Domestic life is the first step of one's cultural and social life, and since all humans love to live with their family and relatives due to their social instinct, the family is the basic unit of society. Social life begins with a clan and family, and a clan is established with the marriage of a male and a female. Because of this, Islam gives equal importance to men and women; each is restricted within defined boundaries and Islam emphasizes the fulfilment of everyone's rights and obligations. Allah Almighty says: "O mankind! We have indeed created you from one man and one woman." (Surah Al-Hujurat: 49,13). The concept of relations, family and clan is found only among humans in creation, and this status is conferred on man, the best of creation, so that he expresses love, respect and kindness to parents, grandparents, siblings and offspring. A man earns and fulfils the needs of the family, and if someone gets annoyed he tries to resolve the issue. All these factors are exhibited due to the existence of a family; therefore, Islam considers the family a beauty for society and a pious community.
questions.explanation: Compiled from the opening sections "The Concept and Meaning of a Family" and "The Beginning of Family and its Social Significance", quoting Surah Al-Hujurat (49:13).

questions.question: Explain the rights and obligations of husband and wife.
questions.answer: The existence and sustenance of humanity is based on the relationship between a man and a woman, so the relationship of husband and wife has an important place among all human relationships. A marriage bond is established after the parents' consent from both sides and the process of requesting and accepting the Nikkah; the Holy Qur'an named this bond "Ahsaun", meaning to be protected within a fortress. Nikkah is an agreement through which husband and wife become lifelong companions and benefactors of one another; they share sorrows and happiness and help each other in difficult times. The Holy Prophet said: "Marriage is part of my Sunnah, and whoever does not follow my Sunnah has nothing to do with me." (Sunan Ibn-e-Majah: 1846). Allah also says: "They (women) are coverings for you, and you are coverings for them." (Surah Al-Baqarah: 2, 187). The Holy Prophet said: "Each of you is a guardian, and each of you will be asked about his subjects." (Sahih Bukhari: 2409). According to Islam there are rights enjoined on both husband and wife for each other; Allah says: "And the women also have rights similar to those of men over them." (Surah Al-Baqarah: 228). The rights of the wife over the husband include the provision of sustenance, dress, home (shelter), medication and other needs as per his financial position. The woman can use the amount of dower in any business within Shariah limitations or keep it to herself. The man is also obliged to behave nicely with his wife and other family members, not to oppress or do injustice in any way, to keep an attitude of benevolence and to fulfil all rights according to Shariah guidance. The wife is responsible for protecting her husband's wealth and provisions like a trust in his absence and should not allow any stranger to enter the home without her husband's permission; Allah says: "So virtuous women are the reverent ones, guarding behind their husbands the way Allah has decreed guarding." (Surah Al-Nisa: 34). She should not demand any expense beyond the financial position of her husband, should not needlessly discuss her difficulties or scarcity of wealth with others (rather she should endure and forgive), should not reveal the secrets of the home, should secure and nurture the children with proper guidance, and should serve her husband and obey him. The Holy Prophet said: "The best of you is he who is best to his family, and I am the best among you to my family." (Sunan Ibn-e-Majah: 2053).
questions.explanation: Compiled from the section "The Relationship of Husband and Wife" and "Obligations and Rights of Husband and Wife", citing Surah Al-Baqarah (2:187, 228), Surah Al-Nisa (34), Sahih Bukhari (2409) and Sunan Ibn-e-Majah (1846, 2053).

questions.question: What is meant by a family?
questions.answer: "Khandan" (family) is a Persian word which means a household, family, tribe, offspring and ancestry; domestic life stands for the gathering of close relatives of a clan. A family includes parents, husband and wife, offspring, grandparents, and paternal and maternal uncles and aunts with their offspring. It is the basic unit of society and the first step of one's cultural and social life.
questions.explanation: Based on "The Concept and Meaning of a Family" section of the lesson.

questions.question: Write about the respect of parents.
questions.answer: The relationship with parents is the most important and respectful of all relations, as they are the means of our life in the world and all our strength is built up due to their care and upbringing; therefore we should not show any negligence in respect and service to our parents. Allah orders us: "And your Lord has ordained that you do not worship anyone except Him, and treat your parents with kindness; if either of them or both reach old age in your presence, do not say 'Uff' to them and do not rebuff them, and speak to them with the utmost respect. And lower your wing humbly for them, with mercy, and pray, 'My Lord! Have mercy on them both, the way they nursed me when I was young.'" (Surah Al-Asra: 23, 24). It is the obligation of the offspring to respect their parents, obey them, serve them and treat them nicely even if they are infidels or polytheists; however, the offspring should excuse if they order something of disbelief or polytheism. It is also instructed to have a good relationship with the relatives and friends of parents, to thank them and to pray for their forgiveness.
questions.explanation: Based on the section "Respect of Parents", quoting Surah Al-Asra (17:23-24).

questions.question: Describe the rights of offspring.
questions.answer: Offspring are the buoyancy of a family; their objective is the sustenance of humanity and they are the great blessing of Almighty Allah. The rights of offspring (which are the obligations of parents) include: good upbringing, arranging quality education and guidance, kindness and affection, marrying them into a good family, maintaining justice in inheritance, giving them necessary religious knowledge, teaching them the knowledge of the Holy Qur'an, the performance of prayers and Islamic values, maintaining equality and justice in treatment, including daughters in love and gifts, not being ungrateful at the birth of a daughter, and avoiding torturing or over-strictness while keeping behaviour of love and tenderness and not killing any offspring due to fear of hunger or poverty.
questions.explanation: Compiled from the section "Rights of Offspring" in the lesson.

questions.question: Write own ten points on the dignity of humanity.
questions.answer: (1) "Dignity" stands for respect, excellence and greatness; the dignity of humanity means each human has respect and greatness in this universe. (2) Humans are titled "Ashraf ul Makhluqaat" — the best creation of Almighty Allah on the earth — and therefore have superiority over all other creations. (3) Allah has created all things on earth, heaven and between them for the benefit and ease of humans, and all things are the collective heritage of humans. (4) The Holy Qur'an declares this honour: "Indeed We have honoured the Descendants of Adam and transported them over land and sea, and gave them good things as sustenance, and made them better than most of Our creation." (Surah Al-Asra: 70). (5) A human receives the blessing of speech, knowledge and wisdom through which he becomes eligible to explain his feelings adequately. (6) Islam negates the differences of caste, colour, language and country. (7) The criteria of greatness and excellence is piety and fear of Allah: "Indeed the more honourable among you, in the sight of Allah, is one who is more pious among you." (Surah Al-Hujurat: 13). (8) All humans in this world are from one origin — from a single soul — as stated in Surah Al-Nisa: 1. (9) Allah has made man His deputy and vicegerent on earth and freed him from the slavery of false gods; no one has superiority over another except in faith, knowledge and piety. (10) Every human should protect the life, respect and property of other humans who belong to the nation and country without distinction of caste, colour, religion and language, and should avoid all acts that are against the dignity of humanity, such as pride, degrading others, oppression and injustice, spying, unequal treatment of offspring, taunting people or using foul language.
questions.explanation: Compiled from the sections "Concept of the Dignity of Humanity" and "Significance of the Dignity of Humanity" and the list of "Actions that are against Dignity of Humanity", citing Surah Al-Asra 70, Al-Hujurat 13 and Al-Nisa 1.

questions.question: What does Holy Quran order us about the dignity of humanity?
questions.answer: The Holy Qur'an establishes the dignity of humanity in very clear terms. Allah says: "Indeed We have honoured the Descendants of Adam and transported them over land and sea, and gave them good things as sustenance, and made them better than most of Our creation." (Surah Al-Asra: 70). This shows that Allah has bestowed very high excellence on humans over all creations and has made all things on earth, heaven and between them for their benefit and ease. The Qur'an also declares that the criterion of greatness is not caste, colour, language or country but piety: "Indeed the more honourable among you, in the sight of Allah, is one who is more pious among you." (Surah Al-Hujurat: 13). It further teaches that all humans are from one origin: "Created you from a single soul and from it created its spouse and from them, both has spread the multitude of men and women." (Surah Al-Nisa: 1). Allah has made man His deputy and vicegerent on earth, released him from the slavery of false gods and made him responsible and dignified, bound to abide only by Allah's commandments. No one has superiority over any other person except in faith, knowledge and piety, and these verses address every human, whether Muslim or non-Muslim.
questions.explanation: The answer quotes and explains the Qur'anic verses (Surah Al-Asra 70, Al-Hujurat 13, Al-Nisa 1) used in the lesson on the dignity of humanity.

questions.question: Describe the concept of dignity of humanity.

Humans are titled "Ashraf ul Makhluqaat", the best creation of Almighty Allah on earth, and therefore have superiority over all other creations. The dignity of humanity means each human should protect the life, respect and property of other humans who belong to the nation and country without distinction of caste, colour, religion and language.
questions.explanation: Taken directly from the section "Concept of the Dignity of Humanity" in the lesson.

questions.question: Write down the conditions which are against the dignity of humanity.
questions.answer: Man has a distinctive status due to piety and good manners, but there are many habits which are against the dignity of humanity, such as: pride (considering oneself superior in knowledge, wealth, caste or wisdom before Allah or creation); degrading people, making fun of them, accusing them or adopting a disrespectful attitude; oppressing and doing injustice to people and finding defects and spying on them; behaving unequally with offspring by distinguishing between younger and older, wise and unwise, and sons and daughters; taunting any human being because of physical shortcoming or error, calling people bad names and disrespecting them; and talking in a bad manner with foul words and unfriendly ways.

questions.question: What sort of social evils emerge when collective justice is avoided?
questions.answer: Collective justice means that every member of society receives his or her rightful due and lives with honour and security. When collective justice is avoided, the whole fabric of society is disturbed. Islam teaches that the root cause of all ills and unrest in society is the abandonment of justice; a society becomes disordered the moment its people forsake justice. The place of justice is then taken by 'Zulm' (oppression), which literally means to place things where they do not belong. Consequently, the weak, the poor and the helpless are deprived of their rights while the powerful and the wealthy are favoured, and this partiality breeds hatred, enmity and class conflict. Wealth becomes concentrated in a few hands, oppression in economic and social dealings increases, and the basic needs of the disabled and unemployed are neglected. Dishonesty, bribery and corruption spread in the courts and administration because law no longer treats all people equally. Social peace and tranquillity are destroyed, mutual trust disappears, and crimes and disorder multiply. In short, avoiding collective justice produces oppression, inequality, corruption, distrust and disorder, and it ultimately ruins both the moral and material life of the community.
questions.explanation: The lesson states that the root cause of all ills and unrest in society is the avoidance of justice and that a society is disturbed when its people forsake justice; the opposite of 'Adl (justice) is 'Zulm (oppression).

questions.question: Suggest some measures to establish collective justice in society.
questions.answer: Collective justice can be established in society by applying the guidance of Islam to every walk of life. First, justice in law must be secured so that everyone is equal in the sight of law and the law prevails over all distinctions of rich or poor, officer or subject, friend or enemy, without any difference between small and big. Second, a strong judicial system ('Qadha' or courts) should be set up and supervised honestly, following the example of the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) who founded it himself and personally assessed the judgement skills of the companions he appointed. Third, the Qur'anic command of Surah Al-Nahl (16:90) to do justice, show kindness and give to relatives must be put into practice, and people should be reminded that Allah orders us to judge between people with fairness (Surah Al-Nisa 4:58). Fourth, in the economic sphere everyone should be free to earn lawfully through trade, agriculture, industry and employment, and the rulers of the Islamic state should provide the basic needs of the disabled and unemployed so that no one suffers financial injustice. Fifth, social justice should be maintained among all tribes, nations and classes, remembering that no one is superior to another except through piety and good deeds (Surah Al-Hujurat 13). Finally, individuals should be educated and trained to give everyone his rightful due without negligence and to remove oppression, so that society enjoys peace and tranquillity.
questions.explanation: The lesson describes forms of collective justice (justice in law, economic life, a just judiciary and social equality) and quotes Surah Al-Nahl 90 and Surah Al-Nisa 58; these point to the practical measures for establishing it.

questions.question: Describe the meaning and the concept of collective justice.
questions.answer: 'Adl' is an Arabic word whose literal meaning is to straighten, equalise, balance or compare two things. The concept of collective justice stands for justice in society, that is, justice among the people of a society in which everyone enjoys his or her rights. To divide a thing into two equal parts, to place everything in its right place, and to deal with a person as he deserves are all part of the concept of justice, while its opposite is 'Zulm' (oppression).
questions.explanation: Directly from the lesson's opening definition of 'Adl (justice) and the definition of collective justice as justice in society where everyone enjoys his or her rights.

questions.question: How does Holy Quran guide about collective justice?
questions.answer: The Holy Qur'an guides about collective justice by commanding believers to live their collective life with justice and kindness. Allah says, 'Indeed Allah decrees justice and kindness, and of giving to relatives, and forbids from the shameful and evil and rebellion' (Surah Al-Nahl 16:90). It also orders, 'Whenever you judge between people, judge with fairness; undoubtedly Allah gives you an excellent advice; indeed Allah is All Hearing, All Seeing' (Surah Al-Nisa 4:58), which means that in judgement friends and enemies, rich and poor, Muslim and non-Muslim must all be treated equally.
questions.explanation: The lesson quotes these two verses (Surah Al-Nahl 90 and Surah Al-Nisa 58) as the Qur'anic guidance for collective justice.

questions.question: What are the manifestations of Modesty and Chastity? Describe with examples.
questions.answer: Modesty and chastity are not limited to a person's character and actions; they also influence his thoughts and his way of speech. Their main manifestations, described in the lesson, are as follows. (1) Speech: it is inappropriate for a Muslim to abuse or talk in obscene words or manners; instead he should either speak good or remain silent, avoid a rude temper and keep away from useless discussions. For example, a modest person controls his tongue and never uses vulgar or offensive language. (2) Dress: Islam has outlined two objectives of dressing, covering and beautification; therefore men and women should wear modest dress that fulfils the standard of Shariah covering, and any dress that is against modesty or resembles the opposite gender is against modesty and chastity. For example, a believing woman observes proper veiling and a man dresses decently. (3) Attitude in daily life: a true believer should avoid an immodest attitude in all his activities; the Qur'an orders men and women to lower their eyes and protect their modesty, and not to look at anything obscene or think anything vulgar, for 'Allah well knows the covert glance and all that lies hidden in the hearts' (Surah Al-Mu'min 40:19). For example, a modest person lowers his gaze and guards his thoughts and desires. (4) Gathering: a person spends much time in gatherings, meetings and celebrations, and during all of these he is bound to retain modesty in his actions, speech and manners. Besides these, the requisites of modesty also include guarding the tongue from offensive words, feeling ashamed of immodest discussion, and recognising the rights and status of others, such as not raising one's voice above a scholar out of respect for his knowledge.
questions.explanation: The lesson's section 'Manifestation of Modesty and Chastity' lists Speech, Dress, Attitude in daily life and Gathering as the practices that must reflect modesty, together with the 'Requisites of Modesty'.

questions.question: Write down a note on the excellence of Modesty and Chastity in the light of the Holy Quran and Hadith.
questions.answer: In the list of Islamic morality, modesty and chastity stand like soul and life. Allah taught modesty to Muslims and declared this great moral attribute the most excellent. The Holy Qur'an, while describing the attributes of true believers, says: 'And who guard their private organs' (Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:5), and such a person is called modest, that is chaste. The Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'Every deen has an innate character. The character of Islam is modesty' (Mauta Imam Malik, Hadith 2634). Another Hadith says: 'Indeed Allah is modest and concealing, and He loves modesty and concealment' (Sunan Abu Dawood, Hadith 4012). The Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) further declared modesty to be a branch of faith: 'And modesty is a branch of Iman' (Bukhari 9, Muslim 30), and stated, 'When you do not have modesty, so do whatever you want' (Sunan Abu Dawood, Hadith 4797). Hazrat Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) reports that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Iman has over seventy branches, and modesty is a branch of Iman' (Bukhari 9, Muslim 30), and Hazrat Abdullah Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) reports, 'Modesty and belief are together. If one of them is removed, the other is removed' (Al-Adab Al-Mufrad 1313). It is also said in a Hadith, 'Al-Haya is from faith, and faith is in Paradise. Obscenity is from rudeness, and rudeness is in the Fire' (Tirmizi 2009). These verses and Ahadith show that modesty and chastity are among the most excellent and beloved virtues in Islam.
questions.explanation: The lesson's section 'Significance and Excellence of Modesty and Chastity' cites Surah Al-Mu'minun 23:5 and several Ahadith (Mauta Imam Malik 2634, Sunan Abu Dawood 4012 and 4797, Bukhari 9, Muslim 30, Al-Adab Al-Mufrad 1313, Tirmizi 2009).

questions.question: What is the importance of modesty in Islam?
questions.answer: Modesty is of the highest importance in Islam, for it is the basis of a person's morality, dignity and chastity. The more a person possesses modesty, the more he dislikes evil; he abides by the commandments of Allah and restrains himself within moral boundaries. Modesty is an attribute of a believer and the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) declared it a branch of Iman (faith); therefore modesty and belief are joined together, and if one is removed the other is removed too. Islam holds modesty so important that it is called the very character of this religion: 'The character of Islam is modesty.' Modesty safeguards a person from the worst transgressions; a person who does not possess this attribute becomes careless about sins and evil-doings and is not ashamed of doing them, and when a person loses his modesty he becomes like a beast that runs after his desires. Modesty, therefore, protects individual character and keeps the whole society pure, respectful and virtuous, and prepares a person as a respectable citizen of society and a prepared person for the Hereafter.
questions.explanation: The lesson explains that modesty is the basis of a person's morality, dignity and chastity, is a branch of Iman, is the character of Islam, and secures a person from the worst transgressions.

questions.question: Describe the meaning and the concept of modesty and chastity briefly.
questions.answer: 'Iffat' (Modesty) is an Arabic word that stands for piety and chastity; in Islamic terminology it means to avoid vulgarity and adultery by controlling evil desires and adopting chastity and moral hygiene. Along with it comes another word, 'Ismat', which stands for honour, sinlessness and pureness. The literal meaning of 'Haya' is shame and modesty; it is a natural and moral attribute that keeps a person away from indecent acts out of fear of Almighty Allah.
questions.explanation: Directly from the lesson's section 'The Concept and Meaning of Modesty' defining 'Iffat, 'Ismat and 'Haya.

questions.question: What is the literal meaning of modesty?
questions.answer: The literal meaning of modesty is shame and self-restraint. The Arabic word 'Haya' literally means shame and modesty, while 'Iffat' means piety and chastity. A person who refrains from indecent actions out of fear of Allah and keeps his desires within moral limits is called modest.
questions.explanation: The lesson states that the literal meaning of 'Haya' is shame and modesty, and that 'Iffat stands for piety and chastity.

questions.question: How is the modesty of the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) described in Ahadith?
questions.answer: The Ahadith describe the modesty of the Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) in very high terms. Hazrat Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) reports that the Messenger of Allah was even shier than a virgin behind her veil, and when he saw something he disliked, they could perceive it on his face. The Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) also declared modesty to be a branch of Iman and said, 'Indeed Allah is modest and concealing, and He loves modesty and concealment', showing that his own modesty was a reflection of this divine attribute.
questions.explanation: The lesson reports the Hadith of Hazrat Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri (Prophet was shier than a virgin behind her veil) and the Prophet's statements about modesty being a branch of Iman and Allah loving modesty and concealment.

questions.question: What did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) say about the greatness of Hazrat Imam Hussain (R.A.)?
questions.answer: The Holy Prophet (peace be upon him) spoke about the greatness of Hazrat Imam Hussain in many blessed sayings. He declared that Hazrat Fatima is the leader of all women in Paradise, and that Hasan and Hussain are the leaders of all the youngsters in Paradise (Tirmizi: 3781). He also said, "Anyone who loves Al-Hasan and Al-Hussain has indeed loved me, and anyone who hates them has indeed hated me" (Ibn-e-Majah: 143). Once, when the Holy Prophet was going to a feast and saw Imam Hussain in a street of Madinah, he moved forward, stretched out his hand to hold him, and after finally holding him and kissing his forehead, said: "Hussain is from me, and I am from Hussain. Allah loves whoever loves Hussain; Hussain is one of my grandsons" (Ibn-e-Majah: 144). When, in his last days, Hazrat Fatima asked him to bestow something upon her two sons, he said, "We bestowed our awe and leadership to Hassan and valour and generosity to Hussain" (Muajam Kabeer Tabarani 8/185). The Prophet thus made it clear that to love Imam Hussain is to love him, and to keep spite against him is to have spite with the Holy Prophet himself.
questions.explanation: The lesson quotes these hadiths (Tirmizi 3781; Ibn-e-Majah 143 and 144; Muajam Kabeer Tabarani 8/185) while explaining the excellence and greatness of Imam Hussain.

questions.question: What do you know about the event of Karbala? Write down a brief note on it.
questions.answer: After Yazeed seized power, the governor of Madinah Munawwarah, Walid bin Uqbah, called upon Imam Hussain to pledge allegiance to Yazeed, but he refused and left for Makkah, where he stayed for four months. Meanwhile the people of Kufa sent him letters inviting him to Kufa so that they could pledge allegiance to him, saying that they had no leader except him and that under the government of Yazeed Islamic values and commandments were being violated. Imam Hussain therefore sent his paternal cousin, Hazrat Muslim bin Aqeel, to Kufa to assess the situation. When Yazeed learnt of his arrival, he deposed the governor of Kufa, Noman bin Bashir, appointed Ubaidullah bin Ziyad in his place, and ordered that Hazrat Muslim bin Aqeel be killed or made captive; Ibne Ziyad got him martyred. Imam Hussain, with his family, left Makkah for Kufa on 8th Zilhaj, 60 A.H., and after a tiresome journey of twenty-four days arrived at Karbala on 6th Muharram, 61 A.H. The commander of Yazeed's army, Umar bin Saad, insisted that Imam Hussain pledge allegiance to Yazeed, and this communication continued from the 2nd to the 10th of Muharram. Imam Hussain, however, clearly denied the pledge of Yazeed and refused to bow down to falsehood. At last, on 10th Muharram, 61 A.H., a battle between truth and falsehood took place in which Imam Hussain was martyred along with his family and devotees in a state of hunger and thirst. In this way he stood firm to uphold Deen-e-Islam and the superiority of truth, and with his great sacrifice he set an example for the whole Muslim Ummah.
questions.explanation: This follows the lesson's section on the 'Refusal to the pledge of Yazeed and Event of Karbala', covering the dates 8 Zilhaj 60 A.H. and 10 Muharram 61 A.H.

questions.question: Describe the ancestry of Hazrat Imam Hussain (R.A.).
questions.answer: The complete name of Hazrat Imam Hussain is Hussain bin Ali bin Abi Talib bin Abdul Muttalib bin Hashim. His father is Hazrat Ali, the Loin of God, and his mother is Hazrat Fatima Zahra, the daughter of the Holy Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). He is Hashmi from both of his parents and therefore enjoys very high excellence in status. His surname is 'Abu Abdullah' and his titles are 'Sayyid ush Shuhada', 'Sayyid Shabab Ahl al-Jannah' and 'Rayhana tul Nabi'; he is also remembered as 'Shaheed-e-Karbala' in the Muslim Ummah.
questions.explanation: Directly taken from the lesson's 'Ancestry' paragraph, which gives his full lineage, surname and titles.

questions.question: How did Imam Hussain (R.A.) correct the ablution of a man?
questions.answer: Once Hazrat Imam Hussain, along with his brother Imam Hassan, was in a masjid where he saw a man performing ablution improperly. Rather than reproach him directly, he said, "Uncle! We are young and we are offering ablution; please indicate if we make any mistake." When the man saw their ablution, he realised that the two youngsters had performed ablution correctly while his own ablution was incorrect. (Bihar al-anwar, Imam Majlisi, V. 43, pg. 319)

questions.question: Give an introduction to the family of Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah (R.A.).
questions.answer: Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah's real name was Amir bin Abdullah bin Jarrah bin Hilal. He belonged to 'Banu Fehr', a branch of the Quraish, while his mother, who accepted Islam, belonged to the Banu Harith tribe. His father was killed in the Battle of Badr as an infidel, and because of the grace of Islam he disliked adding the name of his unfaithful father to his own name; hence, with respect to his grandfather, he was referred to as Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah.
questions.explanation: Taken from the lesson's 'Name and Ancestry' paragraph, which explains his family lineage and why he is known by his grandfather's name. (The exercise prints this section as (A) 'brief answers'; it is recorded here as a short-answer item per the standard section scheme.)

questions.question: When was Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah (R.A.) born? Why did he attach his name with his grandfather?
questions.answer: He was born in Makkah, in the house of Abdullah bin Jarrah Fehri, after 11 years of Aam ul Feel (the Year of the Elephant), and was brought up in Makkah. He attached his name with his grandfather because his father had been killed in the Battle of Badr as an infidel; out of the grace of Islam he disliked adding the name of his unfaithful father to his own name, and so he was known with reference to his grandfather as Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah.
questions.explanation: The lesson's 'Birth' and 'Name and Ancestry' sections give his birth (11 years after Aam ul Feel) and the reason for taking his grandfather's name.

questions.question: Why is he called 'Ameen ul Ummah'?
questions.answer: He is called 'Ameen ul Ummah' (the trustworthy of the Ummah) because when the Christians of Najran surrendered and agreed to pay Jizya, they requested the Holy Prophet to send them a trustworthy person. The Holy Prophet held the hand of Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah and said, "He is the trustworthy of this Ummah" (Sahih Al-Bukhari, 4380).
questions.explanation: The lesson quotes this hadith of Sahih Al-Bukhari (4380) while explaining his excellence, which gave him the title Ameen ul Ummah.

questions.question: Which event occurred in the battle of Saif ul Bahr for the help of Muslims?
questions.answer: In the expedition to Saif ul Bahr (the sea coast), Hazrat Abu Ubaidah bin Jarrah was sent with a company of Muslims who suffered severe hunger during the campaign. Then, by the help and mercy of Allah, a huge creature of the sea was cast ashore, which the Muslims ate and by means of which they were saved from starvation and were helped; this event is remembered as the divine help granted to the Muslims in the battle of Saif ul Bahr.
questions.explanation: This refers to the well-known expedition of Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah to the seashore (Saif ul Bahr) recorded in the hadith literature, where a large sea creature provided relief to the hungry Muslims.

Keep some needful things with you," to which he replied, "O Ameer ul Momineen! Our existing condition of simplicity will lead us to luxurious living very soon" (Musannaf Abdul Razzaq, 11/311). Similarly, after the second conquest of Palestine, when Hazrat Umar came to him for a meal, he presented pieces of dry bread dipped in water, which he was eating himself, showing his extreme simplicity.
questions.explanation: The lesson gives both incidents as examples of his simple, unostentatious lifestyle, citing Musannaf Abdul Razzaq and Sunan Abi Dawood.

questions.question: Describe the services of Jabir bin Hayyan in Chemistry.
questions.answer: Jabir bin Hayyan is remembered in Chemistry as 'The Father of Chemistry'. He did a great deal of experiment in medicine and metalwork, discovered many new inventions, and outlined principles of chemistry that are considered authentic till today. He invented an instrument called 'Qura Anbiq' to extract the essence of herbs and flowers by heating, an instrument that is known today as 'Quranfil' (the alembic). He invented sulphuric acid, hydrochloric acid, carbonate (Armenic) sulphide, the method of making hair colour, the calcination of metal, and the method of iron varnishing. He was the first chemist to divide matter into three categories - plants, animals and minerals - and he further divided minerals into three types: those that evaporate, those that melt in the fire, and those that erupt on heating. Based on his studies and experiments he also invented a liquid made of elements of different metals and chemical reactions that burned things, which was named 'Tezab' (acid) from 'Tez aab'. In this way a new branch of science, 'Chemistry', was founded, and because of these outstanding services he is honoured as the father of the subject.
questions.explanation: This summarises the lesson's 'Scientific Achievements' section, listing his inventions (Qura Anbiq, acids, calcination, etc.) and his classification of matter.

questions.question: What do you know about the books of Jabir bin Hayyan?
questions.answer: Jabir bin Hayyan is counted among those scholars who wrote a very large number of books. The total number of his booklets and books is more than 232; according to one statement he compiled more than 500 books, most of which have been lost and are not extant today. His books were translated from Arabic into Latin and from Latin into English, and it was through them that Europe approached this knowledge and was introduced to Chemistry. Among his books, 'Aidah', 'Al-Khawas al-Kabir' and 'Al-Meezan' are about Chemistry, while his other books deal with astronomy, physics, geometry, philosophy, logic and politics. (Great Scholars of Chemistry, Jabir bin Hayyan, pg. 20)
questions.explanation: This follows the lesson's 'Books of Jabir bin Hayyan' section, which mentions his more than 232 (or 500) works, their translation, and his chemistry-related books.

His ancestors belonged to Khurasan and Tous, and he was born in the tribe Azd in 102 A.H. His father, Hayyan bin Abdullah, had migrated from Syria to Tous and traded in perfume (Itr); Jabir was born a few months after his father opened his perfume shop in Tous, and he acquired his early education there under his father's supervision.

There he devoted himself to acquiring knowledge of Physics, Mathematics and other subjects; the scholars and the people of learning welcomed and honoured him, and this city became the centre where he carried out his scientific work and experiments.

questions.question: Write down the literary and spiritual services of Hazrat Muhammad Rashid Raudhe Dhanni.
questions.answer: Hazrat Muhammad Rashid Raudhe Dhanni was excellent in spirituality and proficient in Tafseer, Hadith, jurisprudence, Sufism, History, Linguistics and other branches of knowledge, and he was very fond of the Persian and Arabic languages. His interest in reading was so high that he always kept some book in hand, and he maintained a substantial personal library; to develop people's interest in reading he would say, "Whoever buys an expensive book, knowledge would not end from his progeny." He always guided people and invited them toward religion, and in his leisure he busied himself with literary works. His famous books include 'Jama al-Jawami' (a Persian dictionary in four thick volumes), 'Aadab al Murideen', 'Maktoobat', 'Shrah Asma ul Husna' and 'Jamio Sindhi kalam', while his disciples compiled his speeches, quotes and life details in 'Malfoozat Sharif Peer Muhammad Rashid Raudhe Dhanni', 'Majma al fiyuzaat' and 'Sohbat nama'. Spiritually, he received his primary training from his father in the Naqshbandiya and then the Qadriya chains, and at the age of 27 he was nominated as the successor of his father. After that he rendered his services in the propagation of Shariah, spirituality, the remembrance of Allah and the spread of the Sunnah. His spiritual compassion benefited thousands; he travelled to Punjab, Kuch Bhooch, Rajhistan, Gujarat, Kathiyawar and Balochistan, benefiting people with knowledge and spiritual excellence. He also worked to eliminate polytheism and innovations in Islam, standing against them in Sindh just as Hazrat Mujaddid Ali Thani and Shah Waliullah Muhaddis Dehlvi had done elsewhere, promoting the Sunnah of the Holy Prophet and illuminating people's hearts with the love of his companions.
questions.explanation: This combines the lesson's 'Spiritual Attachments and Excellence' and 'Literary, Spiritual and military services' sections, listing his books, spiritual chains and preaching services.

questions.question: Why was Hazrat Muhammad Rashid Raudhe Dhanni given the title of 'Raudhe Dhanni'?
questions.answer: It is said that during Ramadan, when Hazrat Muhammad Rashid was an infant, he had a habit of drinking milk at the time of Sehri, and like other fasting persons he would not drink milk throughout the day; then at the time of Maghrib he would go to his mother for milk. Because of this practice of observing the fast from his very infancy, he became famous as 'Roza Dhanni' - the one who fasts. Later on, with reference to his shrine, this name was changed and he became famous as 'Raudhe Dhanni', which means the saint (owner) of a shrine.
questions.explanation: The lesson's birth section explains that his infant habit of fasting gave him the name 'Roza Dhanni', which later became 'Raudhe Dhanni' in association with his shrine.

questions.question: Describe the ancestry of Hazrat Muhammad Rashid Raudhe Dhanni.
questions.answer: His complete name is Syed Muhammad Rashid bin Muhammad Imam Shah, his title is 'Raudhe Dhanni' and his surname is Yaseen. He is the forebear of the famous Syed clan 'Rashidi', and after 36 generations his ancestry reaches Hazrat Imam Hussain bin Ameer ul Momineen Hazrat Ali. The ancestor of his clan was Hazrat Syed Ali Makki, who migrated from his town for the propagation of Islam and settled at 'Lak Aari' near Seewistan (Sehwan), a city of Sindh, because of which the clan became famous as 'Lakyari'. His father, Hazrat Syed Muhammad Baqa Shah Shaheed, was a devout saint and a scholar par excellence of his time.
questions.explanation: The lesson's introduction gives his full name, the 'Rashidi' clan, the descent from Imam Hussain after 36 generations, and the Lakyari settlement of his ancestor Hazrat Syed Ali Makki.

Besides his father, Hazrat Muhammad Rashid acquired knowledge from Hafiz Zain Uddin Mahaisr and Mian Muhammad Akram Ghumro, and for further education he was sent to the famous saint of Shikarpur, Shah Faqeerullah Alavi.
